Sports.title: Pierre Sage faces fight to save Crystal Palace job as dressing room concerns grow
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage is facing a fight to save his job as Crystal Palace manager, talkSPORT understands.

It follows the Eagles' 5-0 defeat to bitter rivals Brighton on Sunday afternoon.

3 Sage could be sacked less than four months after taking charge of Palace Credit: Getty

Palace have won just two of their opening seven Premier League matches under Sage this season.

The Frenchman was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer, replacing Oliver Glasner in the dugout.

However, Palace chairman Steve Parish held reservations over Sage heading into the recent international break.

Despite last weekend's home win over Nottingham Forest, doubts still remain.

There are also concerns within the Palace dressing room following their heavy loss at Brighton.

The result leaves Sage's side two points above the relegation zone in 14th place.

Sage apologised to supporters following the defeat at the Amex after his side were booed off the pitch by the travelling fans.

Speaking to BBC Sport at full-time, he admitted: "Only one feeling, shame. When you play this kind of game you have to show another face. It was our worst face.

"We cannot accept that, especially at the beginning of the game. We didn't fight at this moment. Once it was 3-0 after nine minutes, the game is really different.

"Especially in the way we don't understand in which context we were. In this kind of game you need different ingredients.

3 Sage's side were booed off following a 5-0 thrashing by Brighton Credit: Getty

"It's my fault because I am the coach, I gave the angle to the players. I gave the motivation. I prepare the situations. We played so badly. It's my fault.

"I don't want to speak really individually or thinking about details. I have to analyse what's happened to take a decision.

"At this moment, once the score is [large difference], it's easier to play. It's about bravery. We have to deal with these things from the beginning of the game."

Palace suffered a catastrophic start to the afternoon as they conceded three goals inside the opening 10 minutes.

Those included an own goal from Jaydee Canvot just four minutes into the match.

Diego Gomez then added a second for the hosts from the halfway line.

3 Sage apologised to Palace fans following their latest defeat Credit: Getty

Yasin Ayari, Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood were also on the scoresheet.

The result marks only the second time Brighton have scored five against Palace and the first instance since 1956.

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha delivers Liverpool contract update amid Arsenal transfer interest
Sports.content:
Liverpool are in talks with Rio Ngumoha's representatives over a new contract, the player has revealed.

The teenage winger's current deal expires at the end of next season.

3 Ngumoha's current Liverpool contract expires in 2028 Credit: Getty

Ngumoha could be set to commit his long-term future to the Reds amid transfer interest in the forward.

Arsenal have been linked with a potential move for the England international in recent weeks.

It comes amid a strong start to the new season for the 18-year-old.

Ngumoha has featured eight times in all competitions for Andoni Iraola's side this term.

Those outings have taken his total number of first-team appearances for Liverpool to 38.

Since making his debut aged 16, Ngumoha has also scored twice and provided an assist for the Reds.

Ngumoha contract update

The youngster provided an update on his contract situation following Saturday's win over Brentford.

Speaking to reporters, Ngumoha admitted: "It's all with my agent now. I think it is all going well. I am not too sure.

"I just let the football do the talking, I enjoy playing and all of that is in the back of my mind. I just play for Liverpool and hopefully I can carry on doing well."

Ngumoha appeared as a second half substitute in Liverpool's 2-1 away win over the Bees.

3 Arsenal have been linked with a move for Ngumoha in recent weeks Credit: Getty

He replaced the injured Jeremie Frimpong in the 52nd minute at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Despite beating their nine-man opponents, the Reds remain eight points adrift of Premier League leaders Manchester City in fifth.

Ngumoha is into his third season at Anfield, having joined Liverpool's academy from Chelsea as a 16-year-old in 2024.

Following his breakthrough in the first-team, he was handed his senior England debut back in June.

He has now won three caps for the Three Lions after featuring against the Czech Republic home and away during the recent international break.

Meanwhile, Ngumoha is one of four Liverpool players currently out of contract at the end of next season.

3 Ngumoha has already won three caps for England at 18 Credit: Getty

Alexis Mac Allister, Federico Chiesa and Vitezslav Jaros' deals also expire in 2028.

The Reds also have seven players who could leave the club on a free transfer next summer.

Those include club captain Virgil van Dijk as well as both Alisson and Joe Gomez.

Sports.title: Eberechi Eze given harsh reality check over Arsenal future after ruthless Mikel Arteta act
Sports.content:
Eberechi Eze has been told he may need to accept his role at Arsenal being an impact substitute after a nightmare cameo.

Eze was handed his first start of the Premier League season during the Gunners' 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

3 Eze was hooked at half time during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest after being handed his first league start of the season Credit: Getty

However, the England international was substituted at half time at the City Ground by Mikel Arteta in a brutal decision.

To make matters worse, his replacement, Noni Madueke, was the player to score the late winning goal for the visitors.

In his first half showing, Eze lost possession eight times and failed to complete a dribble while playing off the left wing.

He also misplaced four of his passes and really struggled to make an impact against the deep defensive line of Forest.

And after failing to prove why he deserves a starting place, concerns are rising as to whether he'll ever have a key role.

Will Eze ever become an Arsenal starter?

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Final Word, host Majestic said: "Apart from bodying Spurs last season, he hasn't really set the world on fire for Arsenal.

"I can't help but think that the way Arteta sets his team up, the freedom that Eze needs a player...he doesn't seem like an Arteta player."

That then prompted ex-Premier League boss Alan Pardew to admit he thinks Eze won't ever be a starter in this Arsenal team.

"In the way he sets up his No.10, I don't see Eze getting a lot of action there," Pardew said.

"There's a real defensive side to that No.10 position he likes that Martin Odegaard does and Eze doesn't do.

3 Pardew doesn't think Eze will ever be a starter for Arsenal and that his role may be coming on as a late substitute Credit: Getty

"I think Arteta doesn't feel comfortable with that."

He added: "In certain games, against lesser oppositon, Eze will be given that No.10 position.

"But I've seen him on that left side for Crystal Palace a few times and it's just not him. He's never going to go down the left hand side and whip crosses in, he wants to come and play centrally. He's going to make the game too narrow and therefore you've not got enough width, so it's a problem.

"Arteta took him off rightly, in my opinion, as it just wasn't working.

"In the first instance though, perhaps he shouldn't have started him there, and used him as an impact as a No.10. And I think that will be his role at Arsenal, if they need a goal.

"I don't think Eze is going to be a starter for Arsenal, I think he's a sub and if they need a moment, then the manager can give him the last 10-15 minutes of games."

3 Arteta admitted it was tough for Eze coming up against a deep defensive line, but remained positive on his star Credit: Getty

What has Arteta said on Eze?

Arteta may have taken Eze off at the break against Forest on Sunday, but he remained positive on the midfielder post-match.

The 28-year-old scored for Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday after starting on the left wing against Lille.

“Three days ago he scored a goal, he should have scored three and we were all happy," Arteta told Sky Sports.

He then went on to admit that Eze couldn't find space against Nottingham Forest's deep block, so he had to try a new approach.

"This is football, one day it's brilliant, the next day, especially with attacking players to play against a team that defends with 10 players in and around the box, the nine dropping almost at the edge, it's extremely difficult to get in there and that's it.

"But that's why you need fresh legs, a different profile and try different things.”

Sports.title: Sunderland star claims team ‘became arrogant’ in brutal review amid 11-year low
Sports.content:
Nordi Mukiele unleashed an explosive assessment of his Sunderland team-mates following their latest defeat.

The Black Cats were beaten 2-0 at Bournemouth on Sunday as they dropped into the Premier League relegation zone.

3 Mukiele labelled his Sunderland team-mates 'arrogant' after their fourth successive defeat Credit: AFP

A lacklustre display saw the visitors muster just three shots, with none of them on target.

Meanwhile, defender Kevin Danso was sent off just 17 minutes in after bringing down Evanilson.

It marked the club's fifth league loss of the season, with Regis Le Bris' side winning just one of their first seven matches this term.

In contrast, they did not suffer their fifth defeat last season until January.

Sunderland's run of fourth successive reverses is also their longest losing streak in the Premier League for 11 years.

They last suffered the unwanted feat under Sam Allardyce in December 2015, losing five straight matches.

Errors leading to goals have also become a worrying issue for Le Bris to assess.

Omar Alderete was at fault for Bournemouth's second goal as his back pass sent Evanilson through one on one.

It is the fifth error leading to a goal that Sunderland have committed already in the Premier League this season.

What did Mukiele say?

The manner of their latest setback was not lost on Mukiele, who did not hold back at full-time.

3 Sunderland were beaten 2-0 at Bournemouth amid their worst run of top-flight results since 2015 Credit: Getty

Speaking to Sky Sports, the defender admitted: "This game is what we (have been like) from the beginning of the season, to be honest with you.

"We are not good enough. We deserve to be where we are today, definitely.

"Why? I don't know. Maybe because we became arrogant, this is what I think."

Mukiele, who joined the club on a four-year deal last summer, has played every minute of the Black Cats' last six league outings.

Sunderland's slow start follows their seventh place finish last season on their return to the top-flight.

Following an eight-year absence from the Premier League, they qualified for the Europa League, their first European campaign for 53 years.

3 Sunderland have dropped into the relegation zone after winning just one of their opening seven matches Credit: Getty

It was also their highest finish since the 2000/01 season, when they also ended the campaign in seventh.

Le Bris has found success in the Europa League this term, though.

The Black Cats have won each of their opening two matches, beating AZ Alkmaar and Torreense.

Sunderland face Lech Poznan in Poland on Thursday before hosting Leeds United at the Stadium of Light next weekend.

Sports.title: Manchester United suffer disastrous unwanted Premier League first with Leeds draw
Sports.content:
Manchester United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season after their winless run continued on Sunday.

Michael Carrick's side have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions.



3 United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season Credit: Getty

It follows a 1-1 draw with Leeds United at Elland Road despite United taking a first half lead.

The visitors had opened the scoring through Bryan Mbeumo before they were pegged back after the break by Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

United now sit just two points above the relegation zone in 13th place.



Meanwhile, they have won just one of their first seven Premier League matches this term.

United make unwanted history

It marks their fewest league victories at this stage of a season since the 1986/87 campaign.



United have also made their worst start in all competitions since that season.

On that occasion, Ron Atkinson was sacked in November 1986 before being replaced in the dugout by Sir Alex Ferguson.



His side then went on to finish 11th, which at the time represented their lowest final position since promotion back to the top-flight in 1975.

As for this season, United have won just twice across all competitions, with their most recent victory coming against Sabah in the Champions League on September 10.

Carrick's side were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last month as well as losing to Atletico Madrid in Europe on Tuesday.

3 United were denied a first win in six by Calvert-Lewin's equaliser Credit: Getty



The Red Devils boss will be hoping to avoid going seven matches without a win in midweek.

United face a Champions League trip to Italy to face Como on Wednesday before hosting Bournemouth next weekend.

Carrick's slow start to the campaign follows his appointment as permanent boss at the end of last season.

The former United midfielder signed a two-year deal at Old Trafford back in May.



Carrick reaction

Speaking to talkSPORT after the draw with Leeds, Carrick explained: "I thought it was a really good game today.

"I thought it was an edgy game. There was an intensity about it. There was a bit of feeling in it, we could sense that.

3 Carrick's side have won just twice in all competitions this season Credit: Getty

"That's what we expected, but I thought the boys stood up to it unbelievably well.



"I spoke to them before the game about what this means to the football club, to the supporters, the history and the rivalry.

"I think it's important that we attach ourselves to that and the boys were fully committed today.

"We're disappointed we haven't won the game, but it's a tough, tough game. They test you the way they play.

"If there's any leaks or any weaknesses, it gets found out today and a point is a point, but we can certainly take a lot from it the way we went about it."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals why Lisandro Martinez was substituted at half-time
Sports.content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has revealed why Lisandro Martinez was substitute at half-time against Leeds.

Martinez started for United at Elland Road just days after he launched an angry outburst towards the club's board.



3 Carrick started for Man United a few days after his outburst, but was substituted at half time against Leeds Credit: Getty

The Argentinian centre-back slammed their recruitment after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid.

But Carrick admitted on Friday that the drama following Martinez's comments was 'done' and that he was available for selection.

He went on to start against Leeds for the Red Devils and kept a clean sheet in the first half, as his side went in 1-0 up.



Bryan Mbeumo's goal was the difference and United looked to be on the top, leading their rivals as the whistle blew.

However, when coming back out for the second half, Martinez didn't return to the pitch, sitting on the bench instead.



Carrick replaced the defender with Noussair Mazraoui, with Leeds going on to score an equaliser as the game ended 1-1.

Why did Carrick substitute Martinez?

Speaking post-match, Man United boss Carrick explained the reasoning behind Martinez's half-time withdrawal.



He said: "He felt his thigh a little bit."

Martinez had been spotted hobbling during the first half.

He could potentially now be a doubt for United's Champions League trip to Como on Wednesday, which will be live on talkSPORT 2.

3 Carrick has revealed why he took Martinez off at the break after his side drew 1-1 at Elland Road Credit: AFP

Martinez's angry outburst

Martinez, who has started eight games in all competitions for Man United this season, was not substituted for off-the-pitch reasons.

He was reportedly fined for his outburst, but Carrick was clearly happy enough to keep him in his team on Sunday and only took him off due to his knock.



The 28-year-old targeted United's technical director Jason Wilcox in his rant, which he went on to apologise for.

"I have to control myself a lot," Martinez said on Tuesday. "But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."



3 Martinez was fined by United for his comments about the club on Tuesday, but he started for them again on Sunday Credit: Getty

On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he added: "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more.

"It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Sports.title: Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first
Sports.content:
Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first

Pierre Sage has been warned he could be sacked by Crystal Palace if they risk being sucked into a relegation battle.

It follows the Eagles' heavy defeat to bitter rivals Brighton on Sunday afternoon.



3 Sage's side made a disastrous start to their clash with Brighton on Sunday Credit: Getty

Palace were thrashed 5-0 at the Amex after shipping three goals inside the opening 10 minutes.

Those included an own goal from Jaydee Canvot before Diego Gomez scored a goal of the season contender from the halfway line.

The defeat marks Palace's heaviest loss to Brighton since January 1956 and leaves Sage's side just two points above the relegation zone.



A toxic atmosphere amongst the travelling supporters also saw his players booed off at the final whistle.

Assistant manager Paddy McCarthy did his best to calm the situation as Sage was met with jeers from the Palace fans.



Despite only being appointed in the summer, the Frenchman could now find himself under pressure at Selhurst Park.

Sage under pressure

talkSPORT's Perry Groves admitted Sage is 'done' after the derby defeat.



Speaking to Sam Matterface on GameDay Live, Groves said: "I think Sage is going to be demobbed at the end of this game. He’s done."

Alex Crook echoed the sentiment that Palace chairman Steve Parish could soon consider a change in the dugout.

He explained: "There was that story earlier in the season that Jaydee Canvot, who scored the own goal today, was left out of the team.

3 Brighton secured their biggest win over Palace for 70 years Credit: Getty



"Steve Parish wasn’t particularly happy with Pierre Sage for that decision. So I think there are signs of cracks in the relationship.

"I know Steve Parish came out and did quite an in-depth interview with our colleagues at The Athletic and said it’s going to take time, ‘we’re behind him’, but they are giving away too many chances, no doubt about that.

"I fancy Brighton today, despite the fact they’ve got a dreadful recent record in this fixture, because even though they won last weekend against Forest, Crystal Palace, they should have been out of the game by half-time.

"It was down to Forest’s wastefulness, really, that they ended up getting all three points in that match.



"History tells us that if Steve Parish sees signals that his side are heading for a relegation fight, he will make a change. He did with (Frank) De Boer when he was brought in to change the playing style.

"I think that lasted 10 matches, so at the moment, I don’t think the manager is covering himself in glory."

3 Sage was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer Credit: AFP

What's next for Palace?

Frank De Boer was sacked just four matches into the 2017/18 season after suffering four successive Premier League defeats without scoring a goal.



Sage has already seen his side lose four of his nine matches across all competitions.

The loss to Brighton followed league defeats against both Everton and Ipswich Town so far this term.

Meanwhile, Palace were beaten by Lyon in the Europa League in midweek.

They are once again in European action on Thursday as they travel to Turkey to face Besiktas.



Palace then host Newcastle United in the Premier League three days later.

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: Arsenal beat Nottingham Forest thanks to late Madueke goal, Leeds draw with Man United, Brighton hammer Palace
Sports.content:
'The time has come to hang up the boots'

Saido Berahino has announced his retirement from football.

The 33-year-old striker has called time on his career after 14 years in the game, having played for 11 clubs in total.

He was once tipped to become England's next big thing, having starred as a youngster in the Premier League.

Berahino played 133 top flight games, scoring 23 goals and providing three assists, also playing 84 games in the EFL.

Most of his career was spent at West Brom, while he also had stints with Stoke and Sheffield Wednesday before spending two years in Cyprus and last playing for Tabor Sezana in Slovenia.

Issues off the pitch around transfers and general conduct largely derailed his progress, and now, he's retired from the game.

He wrote on Instagram: "A Letter to the Game Football has given me everything. From the streets of Bujumbura to the Hawthorns, from the Premier League to places I never imagined I’d play — this game carried a young refugee kid through life.

"I want to thank West Bromwich Albion for believing in me when I was a boy. Those years at the club, the goals, the fans, the moments… they will always be special. To every teammate, coach, and supporter who shared the journey — thank you.

"There were highs and lows, mistakes and lessons. I learned that the game can lift you up and test you at the same time. Through it all, football remained my constant.

"The time has come to hang up the boots. My body and my heart are ready for the next chapter. I am proud and grateful to now serve the Burundi national team as a coach. Giving back to the country that made me, and helping the next generation, feels right.

"To my family — you have been my strength. To the fans who stayed with me through every chapter — I will never forget your support.

"This is not goodbye to football. It is simply the end of one story and the beginning of another."

Sports.title: Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson is ejected from game after spitting at opponent in shameful NFL moment
Sports.content:
Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson is ejected from game after spitting at opponent in shameful NFL moment

Buffalo Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson has been ejected from their game against the Las Vegas Raiders after spitting at an opponent on the field.

During the second quarter, the Bills safety approached Raiders tight end Brock Bowers for a heated exchange of words - before spitting in his rival's direction.

The disgusting incident occurred right in front of an official, who quickly flagged the action. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game soon after.

Bizarrely, the Bills safety was seen with a big grin on his face as he made his way back to the locker room following the ruling by the officials.

The incident quickly went viral on social media, with fans calling for the Bills to part ways with the former Philadelphia Eagles star.

'If you can't play Professionally, you don't belong in the NFL or Bills Team', one furious fan wrote on X.

Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson was seen grinning after being ejected on Sunday afternoon

The Bills safety was seen spitting at a Las Vegas Raiders rival during their Week 6 clash

C.J. Gardner-Johnson spits in the direction of Brock Bowers, leading to disqualification pic.twitter.com/8zW4OYIP7o — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026

'Just stupid, disrespectful and selfish. Idiot never learns,' another fan said online.

Meanwhile, one fan wrote: 'Just replace him with someone from the practice squad'.

The shocking ordeal comes just two weeks after Gardner-Johnson sparked a feud with Mike Vrabel after the Bills star derided the Patriots' Efton Chism over his incredible game-winning touchdown in Buffalo.

Chism, an undrafted free agent, made a stunning one-handed catch as New England secured a 29-26 victory earlier this month.

It was just his seventh reception since joining the Patriots in 2025 but it condemned the Bills to a first loss of the season and afterwards Gardner-Johnson dismissed Chism as only a 'practice squad player.'

The Bills safety said: 'An elevated guy made a hell of a catch - [we] probably won't hear from him again.... a practice squad player made a hell of a play.

'That's all I'm going to tell you. You do it again, and he probably won't make it again.'

Gardner-Johnson's comments quickly went viral and when they were put to Vrabel, the Patriots coach did not turn down the chance to poke holes in the safety's own resume.

Some fans called for the Bills to cut Gardner-Johnson after the disgusting on-field act

The incident comes just two weeks after Gardner-Johnson drew the ire of New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, having taken aim at New England star Efton Chism

'For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill,' he told The Greg Hill Show.

Gardner-Johnson was drafted by the New Orleans Saints in 2019 and before joining the Bills, he spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles (twice), the Detroit Lions, the Houston Texans, the Baltimore Ravens and the Chicago Bears.

The Bills are his fifth team since 2024. Chism, meanwhile, has played in 11 regular-season games and has never spent time on the Patriots practice squad.

'Nobody works harder [than Chism]. You love to see players take advantage of opportunities, to help the team win,' Vrabel added.

'He is very well respected, he practices, he is on show team, he takes a million reps, nobody logs more miles or yards or whatever we track than Chis.'

Sports.title: Man United's defence is NOT at a top-half Premier League level - Jason Wilcox and Co kicked the can down the road when it came to bolstering the backline this summer and are paying for it now, writes NATHAN SALT
Sports.content:
Man United's defence is NOT at a top-half Premier League level - Jason Wilcox and Co kicked the can down the road when it came to bolstering the backline this summer and are paying for it now, writes NATHAN SALT

Manchester United have played Hull City, Ipswich Town, Everton, Manchester City, Fulham, Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds United and failed miserably to shut out any of them.

They conceded twice against Hull, shipped two in a win over Ipswich, their only league win at this point in late October, and another two followed at Everton in a dramatic 2-2 draw.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin's goal at Leeds United ensured a third successive 1-1 draw in the Premier League and the second time in three games United have thrown victory away.

By the end, all Lisandro Martinez could do was watch on from the bench with an expression that looked totally unimpressed. Up in the stands there was a shake of the head from CEO Omar Berrada with a frustrated Jason Wilcox alongside him at the final whistle.

Defensively the foundations of this team aren't right. The higher-ups knew that in the summer and kicked the can down the road.

At this rate, with United 16th in the form table across the past four league games, that defensive rebuild won't come as a Champions League club and for that heads would have to roll.

Manchester United remain one of only two Premier League teams without a clean sheet

Director of football Jason Wilcox (third from left) has elected to fix the defence next summer

Of the 20 teams in the Premier League this season, only TWO have failed to keep a single clean sheet. Manchester United are one of them. Newly promoted Ipswich are the other.

That should be surprising. Martinez and his team-mates did not look surprised, though.

After all, they started at Elland Road with a right back at left back, a centre-back at right back, and finished with a right back at centre-back with a right winger at right wing-back and a right back at left wing-back. Square pegs, round holes.

They oscillated between a back five and a back four and yet by the end were grateful to have secured a point.

There's no Luke Shaw, out injured in a totally believable scenario before the season began. There's no Patrick Dorgu who, in truth, isn't a left back. Noussair Mazraoui, back involved after a period out injured, looked predictably uncomfortable and unsure as a centre-back. It was his mismatch from a corner that allowed Leeds to score.

Martinez, after a strong first 45 minutes that represented the best defensive half of United's season so far, was forced off with a knock at the interval. United looked significantly worse without him.

United have an enormously long list when it comes to what they must fix right now.

They must find a way to bring Bruno Fernandes, operating as a false nine here, into form as he once again struggled. They must be clinical when the chances arrive. Carrick must make better decisions in-game, too, with substitutions here failing to make the side better.

United are proving a soft touch at the back and cannot progress by conceding every match

Lisandro Martinez (middle) looked unimpressed as United conceded after his substitution

But crucially, they must become harder to score against. Right now, they aren't – and opponents are smelling blood in the water.

'When you come to places like this, you can't be beaten on set plays and we conceded a set play which got them back in the game,' Harry Maguire, who individually did play well and won Player of the Match at Elland Road, said.

'Throughout we felt comfortable in our [back three] shape. They didn't create too many chances. To concede a set-piece after half-time is disappointing. We had to dig in.'

There are technical complaints and structural ones, too, no doubt. There have been fine margins – the Man City goal at Old Trafford shouldn't have stood, for one.

But in their heart of hearts, these United defenders, however short they have been left by those upstairs (and they have by the way), have got to want to defend and want to become hard to play against.

They simply aren't brave enough. Maguire agrees.

'We're in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for Man Utd we have to have that bravery and composure,' he said.

Laid bare that one of this side's most experienced players, a former captain, explicitly stated that this back-line isn't brave enough. That's as damning as anything Martinez said in the mixed zone after losing to Atletico Madrid.

Harry Maguire, who actually played well, accused United of not being brave enough defending

Let's not forget that this is a backline that has Maguire and Martinez both out of contract in 2027. The club hold the option to extend both and may well do so. But surely both must earn it? Dalot, too, is under the microscope ahead of this supposed defensive rebuild next summer. Shaw is out of contract next June and what of the long-term prospects of players like Mazraoui? The bar by which these players are being judged is getting lower by the week.

Drawing at Leeds means that United have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4, L2), their fewest number of wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87.

Wilcox and Co kicked the can down the road when it came to bolstering the backline and are paying for it now.

'This is not a club at Champions League level,' Martinez fumed in Madrid.

Right now they aren't at a top-half Premier League level.

Fail to fix their defence on the fly and this could get a whole lot worse before it gets better for United.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal's resilience and ability to 'suffer' in gritty victory at Nottingham Forest but makes tactical admission - as Gunners boss lays down challenge to 'special' Noni Madueke after matchwinning cameo
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal's resilience and ability to 'suffer' in gritty victory at Nottingham Forest but makes tactical admission - as Gunners boss lays down challenge to 'special' Noni Madueke after matchwinning cameo

Mikel Arteta hailed the way his Arsenal players managed to ‘suffer’ and break down Nottingham Forest’s defensive ‘Christmas tree’ set-up to earn victory.

Substitute Noni Madueke’s 80th-minute strike sealed the match as Arsenal’s only shot on target, with Arteta’s bench once again coming to the rescue.

The north London club dominated possession with little joy around the penalty area before four second-half changes, including Madueke, helped change the tide.

It’s now six wins from seven in the Premier League for the Gunners who sit in second place, three points behind Manchester City.

Arteta said: ‘We’ve played 11 competitive matches and won 10. So we're going to get a variety of ways to win in many different contexts. We knew today we wouldn't score in the first 20-30 minutes.

’We were going to face a different Forest because they're extremely well covered. They put a Christmas tree (3-4-1-2) there. There's no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy. You have to otherwise generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether it's in open play or with set-pieces.

Mikel Arteta praised his Arsenal stars for 'suffering' to break down Nottingham Forest's Christmas tree-style defence

He hailed Noni Madueke for reaching 'another level' - but says he 'expects' such performances from the match-winning winger

’We didn't even hit the target, which is the difference. And the longer the game goes, we say, “OK, now we have to play a different game because the moment we start to ramp up our level of frustration, the game is going to be really dangerous for us because we're going to take more risks than we should”.

‘I had the belief that the moment the physical level was going to drop, the spaces would be a little bit bigger. And the finishing delivered because the game changed and the context of that game changed a little bit. And then we have to suffer because we had two or three actions that were a bit strange to witness.’

On Madueke’s display, he added: ‘There's a smile on my face because he's a special character.

‘He's just a special guy. He's in a good moment. I think after the break he's showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well in his actions and he's becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’

Goalscorer Madueke was effusive about the impact of Arsenal’s ‘absurd’ bench to get the three points.

Madueke said: ‘We had to dig deep, we know it's difficult to come here. Thank God we were able to get the win and we move on with three points.

‘If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it's absurd so we know that we're going to start some and finish some and for me it's the same mentality every time. I just want to create or score.

‘Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.’

Sports.title: British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE
Sports.content:
British boxing has a world beater in the ascendancy. Daniel Dubois is starting to look like a monster - and he's ready for Oleksandr Usyk, Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury or anyone else, writes JEFF POWELL MBE

'Bring him on,' roared Daniel Dubois when asked if he would like a third fight against the greatest boxer of his generation who has beaten him twice.

Oleksandr Usyk, who is in a state of limbo somewhere between vacating all the heavyweight tiles and semi-retirement, is a genius so may not fall readily into the trap baited on the banks of the Thames in the dark hours of this Sunday morning.

Ukraine's war hero will have watched Dubois annihilate the gallant Fabio Wardley and recognised that Dynamite Daniel is no longer the callow youth he wiped the canvas with a couple of times during his reign as the undisputed world champion.

Promoter Frank Warren is not given to understatement but when he said 'Daniel has matured now' he was only scratching the surface of the transformation.

It may be a stretch to compare Dubois with the once terrifying Sonny Liston but to those rivals wearing the other belts he needs if he is to become undisputed then he is starting to look like a monster.

'I want them all,' said WBO champion Dubois. He was referring to the winner between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December, who will thereby hold a WBA title, as well as IBF and WBC champions Filip Hrgovic and Ajit Kabayel.

Daniel Dubois knocks down Fabio Wardley during his annihilation on Saturday night

Dubois has declared himself ready to fight anyone in the heavyweight division

Their availability, especially that of AJ or the Gypsy King, will be determined no doubt by there being many more millions in the Aladdin's Cave from which Saudi Arabia has helped finance the welcome flux of mega-fights of late.

If so then Warren is promising a 2027 bursting with monthly heavyweight spectaculars as lustily anticipated as Dubois' second demolition of Wardley . At the rapid conclusion of which another packed O2 crowd was switching its allegiance from a love affair with Fabio's romanticised emergence from white collar boxing to realisation that Britain has a world beater in the ascendancy.

One who may be growing, also, into more of a box office star than the monosyllabic Liston ever was. If his accurate bravura prediction of a 'bash and smash' slaughter of Wardley and his most jovial media conference yet which followed are anything to go by.

Having nursed his confidence in the Dubois family cocoon Daniel now has a mansion of his own to live in and a selection of race cars to drive. No more Mister Shy Guy but none the less likeable for that.

The transition to full manhood was rounded off over the two fights with Wardley. This included recovery from two early knockdowns in the first Fight Of The Year battle to a brutal 11th round stoppage victory.

And now the onslaught triggered by a staggering right hand blow only 17 seconds after the first bell which imposed an eight count on the ropes. Followed by an overwhelming TKO in round two. Wham, bam and thank you man. No criticism this time of a delay in calling it off. In flew the white towel, in jumped referee Steve Gray.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua fight each other in December - and Dubois wants the winner

There has been some nagging at the edge of Dubois' triumph. Suggestions that Wardley came back too soon after the second-half beating in May. But if five-and-a-half months is not sufficient time to recover then how long would be? The immortal Joe Louis used to fight once a month, for heaven's sake.

Wardley, honest man that he is, blamed himself. Having lived to fight another day he vows to do better enough to launch a comeback campaign for another world title. Meanwhile Dubois, at 29 last month, heads for the stratosphere as champion of the next generation of heavyweight boxing.

As the new monster of the prize-ring? It took The Greatest Of All Time to stop the Liston beast In his awesome tracks. Might Usyk be the Muhammad Ali in waiting for Dubois? Maybe. Perhaps not since he is the older legend now. It would be fascinating finding out.

The tombstone on Sonny Liston's grave in Las Vegas describes him simply as A MAN. Frank Warren is right about Dubois becoming exactly that.

Sports.title: Northampton's 28-12 win over Cardiff saves some face for English rugby after a reality check in the Champions Cup opening weekend - and Saints have another star in the England mix, writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Northampton's 28-12 win over Cardiff saves some face for English rugby after a reality check in the Champions Cup opening weekend - and Saints have another star in the England mix, writes ALEX BYWATER

After an avalanche of tries dominated the first three rounds of PREM Rugby, there has been much patting of backs within English rugby about the so-called rude health of the country’s top domestic league.

But the opening weekend of the 2026-27 Champions Cup has provided something of a reality check to those who may have got too carried away at the high-octane action.

Thankfully, current champions Northampton were on hand to save some face. After a draw and six losses against the best in Europe, this victory for Phil Dowson’s Saints was the only one for a PREM side across the cross-border competition’s opening salvo.

It hasn’t been a total disaster. Even without success, Gloucester and Exeter impressed against the might of Bordeaux and Toulouse and there is still plenty of time for a European renaissance.

But, perhaps, all is not as rosy in the PREM garden as many might have begun to think. Even against a weakened Cardiff side who had rested a host of their leading Welsh internationals, Northampton had it far from all their own way and failed to notch a try bonus point, even if it must be noted that they too had their star men absent.

Such a scenario didn’t say much for Europe’s apparent lure. ‘The statistics will say only Saints won, but I don’t think the English teams are too far away,’ said Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson.

Northampton Saints beat Cardiff in the first round of the the Champions Cup group stage

‘The change in format makes it quite tricky. I can only speak from my position, but at this point in the season, everyone wants to compete in both the main competitions. If you want to do that, you have to use your squad. At what point do you rotate?’

Northampton’s England regulars Henry Pollock, Tommy Freeman and Alex Coles were all given the weekend off, while No 10 Fin Smith was wrapped up against the elements on the home bench. Facing just a five-day turnaround for their next United Rugby Championship game at home to the Sharks on Friday night, Cardiff left out Wales back-row forwards Alex Mann and James Botham, club captain Liam Belcher and their form forward Taine Basham.

Dowson described Cardiff’s five-day turnaround as ‘bonkers’ and added: ‘How that’s been signed off is nuts.’

Wales great Taulupe Faletau was on hand to make his first appearance for Cardiff since March, but neither team was at 100 per cent. It was a real shame as if both had been at full throttle, this could have been a great  for those who believe in the prospect of a future Anglo-Welsh league.

Both sides paid tribute to former Sale lock Hyron Andrews pre-match after his tragic passing last Friday. Heavy rain arrived simultaneously. The conditions made for a poor first half. Saints scored twice through James Pater and Toby Thame, but there were errors galore.

George Hendy and Alex Mitchell made fine contributions to the effort of Pater, the young full-back who has had a strong start to his first full senior season. Cardiff were unfortunate to have a try for Tom Manz ruled out.

Northampton struggled to get their trademark, free-flowing attacking game going. The wet weather didn’t help. And when Cardiff centre Harri Millard went over at the start of the second half and Jarrod Evans converted, all of a sudden Saints were in a contest.

With his first touch, their replacement scrum-half Archie McParland knocked on. Anthony Belleau then saw yellow, leaving Saints down to 14 and Cardiff pounced immediately, Evans sending Mason Grady over.

Northampton are the only English side to have one in the Champions Cup so far this season

Evans couldn’t tie the scores with the kick. It roused the home crowd from their stupor and their team responded, the impressive Hendy juggling the ball on his way to the line after receiving replacement Fraser Dingwall’s pass.

A Cardiff breakaway saw Hendy race back brilliantly to stop Josh Adams from what looked a certain score. Hendy is yet to win a senior England cap but must surely be in the mix to make their autumn squad.

Dingwall brought the scoring to a close, but Northampton ended up just short of maximum points under Europe’s new rule that means a try bonus is only gained if you score three times more than your opposition. Cardiff coach Corniel van Zyl confirmed his team asked European rugby bosses if they could have moved this game to avoid a five-day turnaround.

The request was denied. ‘I definitely feel like I had to make changes,’ said the South African, who bemoaned his team’s line-out inaccuracies and failure to take their chances. ‘The boys that came in really stepped up.’

Sports.title: Match Of The Day star Kelly Cates can't wipe the smile off her face as she and boyfriend Mark Chapman are seen together for the first time since their romance was confirmed
Sports.content:
Match Of The Day star Kelly Cates can't wipe the smile off her face as she and boyfriend Mark Chapman are seen together for the first time since their romance was confirmed

Kelly Cates couldn't wipe the smile off her face as she walked alongside her beaming boyfriend Mark Chapman on Sunday.

It was confirmed earlier this month that the Match Of The Day pundits were dating after finding love together on the BBC show last year.

And this weekend the pair were seen together for the first time since their romance was confirmed as they arrived at work for MOTD.

Kelly, 51, looked in great spirits as she kept it stylish in a pale pink loose-fitted shirt and dark grey tailored trousers.

Meanwhile Mark, 53, wrapped up in a cream zip up fleece and dark navy jacket.

The couple were seen smiling and laughing together as Kelly pushed her suitcase along the street.

Match Of The Day star Kelly Cates couldn't wipe the smile off her face as she and boyfriend Mark Chapman are seen together for the first time on Sunday amid their romance

It was confirmed earlier this month that the Match Of The Day pundits were dating after finding love together on the BBC show last year

Kelly was preparing to host MOTD on BBC One, while Mark presented daytime sports coverage on Radio 5 Live.

An onlooker told The Sun: 'Mark and Kelly were smiling and laughing together and walking in sync.

'He had his hands in his pockets and she was wheeling a small suitcase. They kept chatting all the way towards the studios.

'They were wearing matching trainers which was quite sweet. She went towards the TV studios and he walked into the radio section, next to it.'

Kelly and Mark became the main co-presenters for MOTD alongside Gabby Logan last season after Gary Lineker left.

While their shifts presenting the show do not overlap, the pair did appear on Celebrity Gogglebox on the same sofa together in July.

It was revealed earlier this month that the pair were dating, several months after they are said to have realised that they had feelings for one another.

It was reported that they started to fall for one another in May. But the Daily Mail's Katie Hind has revealed it was during their time in Atlanta during the football World Cup this summer, while covering England’s ill-fated semi-final against Argentina, that sparks really flew. You can read more about that here.

It came six months after Mark reportedly split from his girlfriend of three years, Clere Collier, an estate agent who lives in Dubai, who then accused him of becoming close with his co-host.

He insists there was no overlap between the relationships and that he had remained faithful.

Mark was married to his wife Sara for 19 years until she died aged 44 in 2020 after a battle with cancer. They had three children.
