World.title: Full list of public swimming pools now open in Joburg
World.content:
Joburg has reopened more public swimming pools ahead of summer, with 13 more scheduled to be open by Monday.

However, 26 pools across the metro are still undergoing repairs and maintenance, according to the City’s office for Community Development

As of Wednesday last week, the number of operational facilities increased from 13 to 20.



The City is targeting another 13 openings by Monday, 19 October. If successful, this would bring the total number of operational swimming pools in Joburg to 33.

“With most major hurdles substantially resolved, the City’s focus has shifted towards maximising operational capacity,” said Community Development MMC Thapelo Amad.

“This includes sustaining uninterrupted operations, maintaining safety standards and ensuring reliable service delivery ahead of the peak swimming season in November and December.”

The City also confirmed that qualified lifeguards and cashiers are available at Joburg’s reopened facilities.

Which Joburg swimming pools are now open?

The following 20 municipal swimming pools were listed as operational as of the 13th of October:

REGION SWIMMING POOL A Rabie Ridge B Linden B Verity Park B Roosevelt Park B Blairgowrie C Florida Lake C Davidsonville D Jabulani New Pool D Orlando D Pimville D Meadowlands D Noordgesig E Zoo Lake E Paterson Park F Pioneer Park F Rhodes Park G Lenasia South G Eldorado Park Extension 4 D Eldorado Park Extension 9 G Lenasia Extension 2 – Greyville

Public pools scheduled to be open by 19 October

The City identified a further 13 pools for scheduled openings between 14 and 18 October.



“Our phased in approach of reopening swimming pools is working and we anticipate opening 13 additional swimming pools by Monday 19 October, bringing the total to 33,” Councillor Amad announced.

Region Swimming pool D Dobsonville D Jabavu D Diepkloof D Power Park D Senaone E Sydenham E East Bank F Turffontein F Forest Hill F Crown Gardens F Yeoville F Malvern G Lenasia Extension 10

Despite the progress, operational challenges continue to hamper the reopening of certain municipal pools in Joburg.

Coronationville’s pool reopened but had to close again due to an electrical supply issue. Roodepoort’s pool has been affected by a faulty substation, while electrical damage and cable theft have delayed the opening of Florida North swimming pool.

Ivory Park’s newly-completed facility remains closed amid community-related employment demands and security concerns.

Meanwhile, Drieziek’s new public swimming pool is expected to open once snag-list items have been completed.

The City noted that 26 pools across Regions A to G were still undergoing repairs and maintenance, with contractors on site and a number of facilities nearing completion.

“Aquatics will continue monitoring facility readiness, and facilitating further swimming pool openings,” Amad added.

“We will continue engagements with community stakeholders to urgently resolve employment, vandalism and security problems.”

World.title: All grown up! Charlize steps out with two daughters [video]
World.content:
Charlize Theron and her two daughters Jackson and August. Images via IG

Charlize Theron and her two daughters turned heads at the Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles on Saturday, 17 October.

The South-African born actress adopted Jackson (who now identifies as a girl) and August in 2012 and 2015, respectively.

CHARLIZE THERON AND TWO DAUGHTERS TURN HEADS AT EVENT

On Saturday, Charlize made an appearance at the Sixth Annual Academy Museum Gala in LA, where she received the Icon Award in celebration of her cinematic career.



While the blonde Benoni-born star walked the red carpet alone, she shared a sweet moment with her daughters, Jackson, 14, and August, 12.

Charlize and her model-like kids shared a warm embrace in a video captured by People magazine.

Both girls had their hair styled in long braids and wore black minidresses and strappy heels.



While they aren’t biologically related, it’s clear the girls inherited their style and grace from their South African mom.

WHY SHE CHOSE TO ADOPT

Over the years, Charlize Theron has spoken openly and honestly about her unconventional path to parenthood.



In an interview with Elle Magazine in 2018, the South African-born star revealed that she was intrigued with adoption from a young age.

She shared: “South Africa, orphanages were everywhere, and I wanted a brother or sister. I was always aware that there are so many children in this world who don’t have families. Adoption is a very personal thing – I know people whom I love dearly who don’t feel that they could raise another child as their own. I respect that.

“But for me -and I can’t be the only person out there- I never saw a difference in raising an adopted child versus my own biological child. I don’t feel like I’m missing out on something.



“This was always my first choice, even when I was in a relationship. I was very honest with my partners that I was open to having my own biological kids but that adoption had to be a part of my life. I felt that strongly about it”.

World.title: DA and ANC gunning for Cape Town
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The race for Cape Town’s mayoral seat is heating up ahead of next month's polls.

ANC representative Jerimia Thuynsma claims the party managed the metro better than the DA when it last governed Cape Town before 2006.

The parties were facing off in eNCA's We The Nation election debate.

Thuynsma said, "The ANC governed the city for three years, and our delivery record in the three years is clearly much better than the DA. That's why you will be able to see that we delivered more houses... "We were in the process, as I indicated the last time, of getting people who are living in rental stock of the ANC to transfer the houses to them so that they can have ownership and have property that they can basically use. That of course got stopped when the DA came into power in 2006."

Geordin Hill-Lewis blasted the ANC, saying the only example of success that the ANC government can point to is more than 20 years ago.

World.title: DA rejects claims multimillion N2 wall signals failure to develop communities
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Democratic Alliance (DA) has defended the City of Cape Town's plans to build a wall along the N2 highway.

Additionally, it rejected critiques which suggest the project is an admission of failure to transform and develop communities affected by crime.

Speaking at the We The Nation Election debate in Cape Town on Sunday, Cape Town mayoral candidate Geordin Hill-Lewis insisted that it's an anti-crime project.

"Not at all. The fact of the matter is that it is far too easy for pedestrians and people with malign intent to access a national highway. It cannot be that easy to access the national highway," he said.

He pushed back on suggestions that there are reactionary motives for this move.

"There are political parties and political commentators who ascribe or impute different motives to something. But that's their issue. That's not our issue," he said.

The City has allocated R114-million in its adjusted budget for the N2 Edge safety project.

The wall along a 9km stretch of the N2 is meant to improve safety in tandem with beefed-up highway patrolling.

World.title: Can ordinary South Africans afford to live in Cape Town? DA, FF Plus debate
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Cape Town may be the most sought-after place to live in SA, but questions still remain: Can ordinary people afford to live there?

This was the question posed at the We The Nation Election debate in Cape Town on Sunday to the Democratic Alliance (DA), African National Congress (ANC), Freedom Front Plus (FF Plus) and the African Christian Democratic Party (ACDP).

Freedom Front leader Corne Mulder is of the opinion that it's increasingly unaffordable to live in the mother city.

Mulder, who has lived in Cape Town for 30 years, questioned the city’s approach on municipal rates and taxes.

READ | ANC still quiet on mayoral candidates weeks before polls

In his view these disproportionately affect residents who do not fall within the majority that are shielded from the increases.

But the DA pushed back.

Cape Town mayoral candidate Geordin Hill-Lewis defended the city’s record on municipal costs and governance.

Hill-Lewis says Cape metro residents are getting far more value for their municipal rates compared to the City of Johannesburg and City of eThekwini.

“The big difference is that in those cities, the value of your home is being destroyed by bad governance. In this city, the value of your home is being greatly increased and improved by good governance,” he said.

Hill-Lewis conceded that Cape Town is expensive but attributed the increase in housing prices to the demand on housing due to the large number of people moving to Cape Town.

READ | Residents must stay in touch after elections

He said efforts are being made to build more homes and make development accessible.

"You have parties like the Freedom Front Plus who want the best of both worlds. They believe in having their cake and eating it. They want no rates increases, but they want better services that have to be funded.

"They want more cheaper accommodation but also oppose the building of anything in Cape Town. So those are all mutually exclusive positions. They can't actually have the best of both worlds. That shows their lack of experience, the lack of governance credentials, the lack of ability to actually govern," he said.

World.title: ANC still quiet on mayoral candidates weeks before polls
World.content:
CAPE TOWN -With just over two weeks to go before South Africans head to the polls, the ANC is yet to announce its mayoral candidates for the November 4 local government elections.

During this week's We The Nation Election debate in Cape Town, the ANC's Jerimia Thuynsma said it's not his place to make the announcement.

'The responsibility of announcing the mayoral candidate is not mine, it is the national executive committee of the ANC, and they have indicated that they will do it," he said.

The party initially committed to announcing its mayoral candidates in September, after failing to do so in August.

But that month has come and gone, and no announcement, or at least an indication of when it'll do so, has yet been made.

On 6 October, ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula said the party has concluded interviews and will be revealing those who have the potential to be mayoral candidates soon.

World.title: 'I don't think he'll get bail' - expert on Suliman Carrim
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Controversial North West businessman Suliman Carrim’s bail hearing continues on Monday.

He was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport on Thursday for allegedly contravening the Commission's Act after repeatedly failing to appear before the Madlanga Commission.

Security Strategist Andy Mashaile said Carrim's case is complex.

"There's a tall mountain to climb in trying to convince the court, as well as South Africans. You were too sick to testify at the Madlanga Commission, but you are fit to fly.

"These are some of the dynamics in just positioning the two scenarios of him being sick to appear before the Madlanga and him being fit to fly.

"I don't think he will get bail tomorrow, given the dynamics in the ecosystem around him. Those huge voluminous bags and the one-way flight ticket and just positioning it with whether it will aid his integrity and honesty.

"If he had engaged with them, he would not have been at the airport. And if he had bought a return ticket before his arrest, it would have added value or it will add value in the magistrate considering that."

World.title: TRC Inquiry postpones Zuma testimony pending recovery
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The TRC Cases Inquiry will wait until Jacob Zuma is well enough to testify.

The former president is taking time to rest after a hospital stay for what his party calls fatigue.

Meanwhile, it has said Thabo Mbeki is fully cooperating with the commission.

This is despite his multiple attempts to have Chair Sisi Khampepe removed.

The inquiry is looking into claims of political interference to block prosecutions of apartheid-era crimes.

Inquiry spokesperson, Lionel Adendorf, said Monday will be an important day of testimony.

" Tomorrow is an important day. I need to stress that it is, obviously the president because of the time period where the TRC cases inquiry our terms of reference start. It is important that we had to have the president on the stand. Unfortunately our work has been delayed by the review application to the Johannesburg High Court and then the Constitutional Court.

"But here we are. Finally, we will have former president on the stand and we have his cooperation. There was no subpoena issued. He generously and graciously offered to assist us as well as former president Zuma. Our evidence leaders have been in contact with his lawyers.

"We do have an arrangement to interview him at a time when he is much better and able to travel and take the stand. And we hope that we can agree on that urgently. The agreement between our evidence leaders and the legal representatives for former president Jacob Zuma has agreed that it would be done within our timeframe."

World.title: KuGompo City residents fight back
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - KuGompo City residents are taking the fight against cable theft into their own hands.

Resident Chris Botha said Cambridge is frequently plunged into darkness due to the theft of electricity infrastructure.

Cambridge West residents said criminals hide in thick bushes and often use them as hideouts while hacking away at copper wire cables.

One such resident is Anelisa Mbokomba.

"We're experiencing this every week, cable theft every single week, and it goes for the longest periods of two to three days without power.

"We find ourselves having our fridges go bad, unable to do the basic things that we have to do, get our kids ready for school, get ourselves ready for work, just because we have no power," she said.

The Cambridge Sector Four CPF patrols day and night.

They believe communities in the Buffalo City Metro are under siege as cable theft has become out of control.

Cambridge Sector Four's Chris Botha said: "The guys that target the cables or that dig them up, especially, they're not just targeting live cables; they're targeting the backup cables. So not only are your main lines affected, but the backup lines as well, from what we've seen."

The Hawks in the Eastern Cape say that while they acknowledge that cable theft is rife in the Buffalo City Metro, they deny claims made by the residents that law enforcement agencies are losing their fight against the crime.

"I wouldn't say we are not doing enough because we have made a lot of arrests regarding cable theft. Communities are equally responsible for reporting any suspicious activity in their communities. We are trying our best," said Hawks Eastern Cape spokesperson, Ndiphiwe Mhlakuvana.

World.title: Moi family ordeal as armed GSU officers occupy Eldoret property
World.content:
Gideon Moi’s family’s disputed property near Eldoret State Lodge. [Peter Ochieng, Standard]

For nearly a year, private security guards had watched over the five-acre property near the Eldoret State Lodge, going about their daily routine without incident.

But on Friday morning, that routine was abruptly interrupted when armed General Service Unit (GSU) officers arrived and ordered them to leave by 4 pm.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Even LinkedIn is getting tired of your AI-written posts
World.content:
New York — Bland, AI-generated posts have made LinkedIn the butt of many an internet joke this year. The platform has heard its users’ complaints about lengthy, generic missives never touched by human hands loud and clear.

As AI has made it easier than ever to create huge volumes of content cheaply and easily, that “slop” has flooded the internet. YouTube, Pinterest, Spotify and other platforms have all sought to limit the amount of spammy, AI-generated content their users see.

But LinkedIn has been hit especially hard. Scrolling through the professional networking site earlier this year could mean being bombarded by bullet-pointed lists accented by emojis, references to “B2B sales,” and asks for a follow or comment for more.

A report published in July by Pangram, a research firm that tracks AI content online, found that more than 40 percent of long-form posts on the platform were AI-generated, compared to around 30 percent on X and Medium and a smaller percentage on Reddit and Substack.

So now, LinkedIn is upping its fight against slop.

“I know you think you’re doing the right thing with your perfectly bulleted list and your hook at the top, and you followed all the advice from LinkedIn advisors across the internet,” LinkedIn Editor-in-Chief Dan Roth, who leads the platform’s content strategy, told CNN in an interview. “But what works is being human.”

There is some irony in this, given that LinkedIn is owned by Microsoft. The tech giant has pushed for people to adopt its AI tools for everything from writing to coding, and it is up against steep competition from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic. LinkedIn previously offered AI tools to edit or rewrite posts, although it recently scaled the offerings back.

But low-quality AI posts are a business problem for LinkedIn. They all start to sound the same, Roth said.

If users see too many generic AI posts, instead of content that really teaches them something or gives them a deeper understanding of a professional connection, LinkedIn risks losing them to other platforms.

Fighting AI slop

In August, LinkedIn rolled out a button letting users flag when a post “seems like AI slop,” which was clicked more than 1 million times within its first two weeks. Now, the company is trying to use its own AI systems to help weed out AI slop on the platform and to remind LinkedIn users how to post like humans.

The company built a team largely made up of former journalists and social media experts who have an eye for recognizing generic, sloppy content. These experts help train LinkedIn’s AI model on what authentic, useful posts look like. If the model flags a post as low-quality, AI-generated content, it’ll be less likely to be distributed beyond that user’s direct connections.

The LinkedIn office on July 26, 2023, in San Francisco, California. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Also key to the strategy is a creator management team that acts as “content therapists” for executives, subject matter experts and other LinkedIn users, many of whom have gotten accustomed to the convenience of using AI to write what, on the surface, appear to be polished posts, Roth said.

“A lot of times now today, they’ll run it through Claude or Gemini or wherever, they’ll post it on LinkedIn and it will perform poorly. And then they come to the team and they’re like, ‘Why did this do badly?’” Roth said. “And the best thing you can do is give it back to them and be like, ‘Did you enjoy reading this? Do you see yourself in this?”

Instead, the team encourages users to embrace imperfection in their posts — to make videos by leaning a phone up against a coffee mug, rather than shooting in an expensive studio, or to dash off a post to start a conversation, even if it isn’t a complete thought.

The efforts are showing early signs of success. Improvements to LinkedIn’s detection systems have resulted in a 40 percent decline in views of content classified as AI slop, the platform said last month.

That’s not to say LinkedIn is entirely opposed to AI, Roth said, adding that “not everyone is a born communicator.” But failing to edit or personalize content means it’s less likely to reach a wide audience on the platform.

“We just try to push people to be more human,” he said. “That is what is required to be able to cut through the noise.”

World.title: Zelensky praises ‘real leaders’ in Europe as his relationship with Trump deteriorates
World.content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky praised “real leaders” in Europe at a summit in Belgium on Friday, taking a veiled swipe at US President Donald Trump amid testy relations between Kyiv and Washington.

European leaders are rallying around Zelensky after the White House heaped pressure on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil facilities, even as Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continue unabated.

Ukraine halted strikes on Russian oil refineries for three days after Trump’s surprise announcement on Sunday of an “energy ceasefire” between the two countries, but has since resumed attacks given Russia did not reciprocate.

Trump, who is desperate for soaring global diesel prices to ease ahead of next month’s midterm elections, blindsided European leaders last week when he struck a deal allowing Russian diesel exports – a move Zelensky said had left him feeling betrayed.

The US president has blamed the rise in fuel prices on the Ukraine-Russia war, eager to deflect attention from his war in Iran which remains deeply unpopular with voters.

On Thursday, Trump once again lashed out at Zelensky in an interview with Newsmax, saying he found him “more difficult to deal with than Putin.” The following day, he walked back on his comments, saying said he had a “good” relationship with his Ukrainian counterpart. “I want him to do one thing,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “Settle the war,” he said.

As Zelensky arrived at Friday’s summit in Brussels, flanked by the European Union’s top leaders, he didn’t mention the deterioration in US relations, but was keen to emphasize the strength of his relationship with the EU.

“I’m so thankful that we have such huge support from (the) EU Council, Commission and leaders – real leaders – so that they stay with us from the very beginning of this war,” Zelensky said as he walked into the summit.

Starlink services not fully restored

Difficulties for Kyiv have mounted this week, with the country reporting restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink internet service.

Zelensky said on Friday that the Starlink operations had improved but had not yet been fully restored.

“They disrupted logistics and compromised the protection of the civilian population. That’s why this is very troubling,” Zelensky said, noting the military relied on Starlink-equipped drones, which need to move at a high speed, to deliver food and water to troops on the frontline.

“Have we fully restored the speed we had before? No. Is the speed coming back? Yes,” he added.

Trump on Friday said he was not behind the Starlink disruption, telling reporters at the White House, “I didn’t do that. No, we didn’t do that at all.

“It wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon (Musk). And from what I understand, it’s the same as it’s always been,” he said.

Trump added that he wasn’t sure there were any speed restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starshield.“I don’t even think it was slowed down. But from what I understand… We didn’t slow it down at all. And I think it’s probably functioning,” Trump said.

Musk said earlier this week that any decision to limit Starshield was up to the US president. A senior US official told CNN that Trump had made no such request.

The Ukrainian government said on Tuesday that it had not received its usual early warning from the US before a Russian ballistic missile struck a major power plant in Kyiv and damaged a residential building.

But Trump insisted that the United States had not stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

Amid a challenging week diplomatically, Ukraine has also run out of missiles for the US-made Patriot air defense system, a source familiar with the situation told CNN on Thursday.

“It’s an open secret that we are not a priority destination for these missiles now,” Zelensky told Friday’s news conference, noting that most Patriot interceptors were now being sent to the Middle East. But he added that Ukraine was grateful to the Europeans “who are financing all of this,” as well as to NATO and to the White House.

Silence speaks volumes

When a reporter asked whether he thought Trump was treating Ukraine as a scapegoat for his own problems given high fuel prices and the ongoing Iran war, Zelensky paused for a full 15 seconds. With a smile, he told the silent room: “This is my answer.”

Earlier the Ukrainian president said his team was in constant contact with US negotiators and would arrange a meeting in the coming days.

“We will keep living, fighting, and most importantly, living with dignity,” he added. “When the quality of life is so terrible during wartime, maintaining dignity is a very important thing.”

EU leaders said they were preparing a new package of sanctions against Russia – the 22nd package since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In contrast with the Trump administration, they were keen to stress that sanctions against Moscow would be strengthened unless Putin stops the war.

“We supported President Trump’s energy ceasefire, but we’ve seen that Russia did not respect it – not a single minute. Instead, Russia escalated, and therefore we have to increase the pressure on Russia,” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said.

Trump said on Friday that he is waiving a number of sanctions related to Russia, days before they were to take effect under a bill he signed into law last month.

The legislation would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on – among other things – all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, the sale of which is crucial to funding the Kremlin’s war machine.

They were included in the Graham Act, legislation named after former Senator Lindsey Graham, a noted Russia hawk who died in July.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said earlier Friday that Zelensky has “no desire” for a peaceful resolution, adding “on that point, we are in complete agreement with President Trump.”

In a visit to a military command post in an undisclosed location, Putin vowed to continue the war.

“In response to strikes by the Kyiv authorities against our industrial and fuel-and-energy sector facilities, the Russian Armed Forces continue to carry out strikes against Ukraine’s military-industrial complex and infrastructure facilities,” Putin said, according to a video released by the Kremlin on Friday.

The video shows Putin wearing military uniform and greeting senior Russian commanders.

CNN’s Victoria Butenko, Anna Chernova and Kit Maher contributed to this report.

World.title: Pope Leo leads Sunday prayers in first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Rome — XIV has made his first major public appearance since his lung cancer surgery, saying the experience brought him closer to all those who suffer, from the same spot in the Vatican he announced a week ago he needed an operation. Pope Leo XIV has made his first major public appearance since his lung cancer surgery, saying the experience brought him closer to all those who sufferfrom the same spot in the Vatican he announced a week ago he needed an operation.

The 71-year-old pontiff lead the Sunday Angelus from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St. Peter’s Square, where thousands gathered to clap, sing and hear his message.

Leo thanked doctors for his treatment and for all those who prayed for him, adding that he is gradually returning to his duties as pope.

“This experience has given me a profound sense of closeness to all those who are going through illness or a state of infirmity,” he told crowds.

“Now that this delicate phase has passed, I will gradually resume my activities – always with the help of God and your prayers. Thank you once again,” he added.

The pope’s remarks came as thousands of runners taking part in the Rome marathon had been jogging up the main walkway leading into St. Peter’s Square taking a right past the papal residence of the Apostolic palace.

At midday, however, all eyes were on Leo XIV when he appeared at the window of his home to address the crowd, wishing them a happy Sunday in a firm and strong voice.

Nuns wait in St Peter’s Square before the Angelus prayer, a day after Pope Leo XIV returns to the Vatican following surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, on October 18, 2026. Andreas Solaro/AFP/Getty Images

The pope was released on Saturday from the Gemelli hospital following lung surgery to remove a growth which was later diagnosed as an adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

Doctors say he has made a good recovery following his surgery, even saying he can make trip to Latin America due to take place 6-17 November.

“I would say there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place,” Professor Stefano Margaritora, who operated on the pontiff, told Vatican news.

Last Sunday the pope made his surprise announcement that a “nodule” had been found on his lung, and he was going to have surgery. The news of the cancer diagnosis on Tuesday shocked people inside the Vatican and across the Catholic world, given the pope was known for being in good physical shape.

The pope’s visit to Latin America includes Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Leo served as a missionary and bishop in Peru for a number of years. His itinerary includes a stop in Cusco, which is around 3,350 meters above sea level, where there is roughly one-third less oxygen available per breath compared to sea-level.

Sharon Braithwaite and Barbie Latza Nadeau contributed reporting.

World.title: Trump and Netanyahu’s once blossoming bromance sours at a pivotal moment for both men
World.content:
For years, Israelis driving the country’s highways in the final weeks of an election have seen the same image: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu standing beside President Donald Trump, under the slogan, “A different league.”

Less than two weeks before the October 27 vote, the billboards of Netanyahu are back.

This time, Trump is not on them.

The president still appears in some videos for Netanyahu’s Likud party, but his absence may signal something beyond advertising.

Trump has so far declined to endorse Netanyahu and has sidestepped questions on whether he should be reelected.

“I’m not involved in [Israeli] politics anymore,” he told Time earlier this month. On Thursday, Trump told Newsmax Netanyahu would like him to be involved in the election. “I’ve had a very good relationship with him,” he said, but avoided endorsing him again. When asked directly whether he trusts Netanyahu, he said bluntly, “I don’t trust anybody in the world of politics.”

For a campaign that has traditionally treated Netanyahu’s intimacy with the White House as a major electoral asset, the restraint is notable.

Trump has starred in Netanyahu’s campaigns since 2013, when still a businessman and TV personality, he released a video urging Israelis to “vote for Benjamin.”

When Trump entered the White House in 2017, he showered Netanyahu with political gifts.

About two weeks before Israel’s April 2019 election, Netanyahu was in Washington to watch Trump sign a historic proclamation recognizing Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights. In January 2020, five weeks before Israelis went again to the polls, Trump unveiled the Israeli-Palestinian “Deal of the Century” plan. Netanyahu stood smiling by his side.

Ahead of this election, there has been no red carpet. The last time Netanyahu and Trump met at the White House in August, there were no cameras. The two did not meet at all when Netanyahu traveled to New York for the UN General Assembly in September.

Demonstrators protest against Netanyahu’s address to the UN General Assembly in New York in September. His efforts to undercut peace talks have drawn bipartisan ire. David Dee Delgado/Reuters A protesters against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s policies is arrested after blocking a street next to the United Nations. Spencer Platt/Getty Images

Over the course of the last year, Netanyahu has taken steps that have drawn fury from Trump, including undermining Trump-led peace efforts by striking inside Lebanon and Gaza.

Trump has cursed the prime minister out in phone calls and warned him he’s losing support among Americans, according to people familiar with the conversations. He’s asked why Israel was blowing up apartment buildings in Lebanon and warned about the risk of a global economic downturn as a result of the Iran war.

Inside the White House, many of the moves were interpreted as election-year posturing by Netanyahu, whose internal politics are well known by Trump and his advisers. Over the summer, many Trump advisers came to the conclusion that Netanyahu was trying to prolong the Iran war to bolster his own political standing.

Trump has given Netanyahu a degree of leeway because of those political concerns, people familiar with the matter said. But he’s still grown frustrated at some of Israel’s actions, many of which he believes run counter to American interests.

Another person close to Trump suggested his lack of endorsement is tied to Netanyahu’s weakness in the polls. Trump has long been careful to avoid endorsing candidates who seem likely to lose.

In conversations over the past several months, Trump has quizzed Netanyahu about the election and his prospects, according to people familiar with the matter. While Netanyahu has sought to project confidence, Trump is well aware of the prime minister’s difficult political position.

As Netanyahu’s standing fell in the Trump administration, so did Trump’s standing in Israel.

According to Israeli sources close to Netanyahu, Trump was originally meant to be a centerpiece of Netanyahu’s campaign. Last December, at Mar-a-Lago, the prime minister announced that Trump would become the first non-Israeli to receive the prestigious Israel Prize. Netanyahu aides hoped Trump would accept the prize in person at Israel’s Independence Day ceremony in April, giving jumpstarting the campaign.

Then came the war with Iran.

A smoke plume rises following a missile strike on a building in Tehran on March 1, 2026. Atta Kenare/AFP/Getty Images

The joint US-Israeli attack began on February 28 with the two leaders projecting strategic harmony. Netanyahu thanked “my friend, President Donald Trump,” calling him “a leader who stands by his word.” Trump described the two of them as “war heroes” and publicly demanded that Israel’s president grant Netanyahu a pardon in his ongoing corruption trials.

But Trump never showed interest in attending the Israel Prize ceremony. By then, the fighting in Iran had ended and ceasefire talks were underway.

The Iran ceasefire and subsequent memorandum of understanding were deeply unpopular in Israel, particularly on the right. Yinon Magal, a pro-Netanyahu TV anchor, called Trump a “loser” after the deal was signed.

A July survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that only 7% of Israelis had “a great deal of trust” that Trump “will do the right thing” on US-Israel relations, and 45% had none.

“Trump’s stock in Israel, especially among right wing-voters, has weakened,” a Likud source said. “An endorsement would not necessarily have helped Netanyahu so much, so he did not invest much in it.” Another Likud source said, “It’s not as if Trump will endorse any other opponent, so it’s nice to have, but not a must.”

US President Donald Trump leaves the stage after speaking during a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum on October 07, in San Antonio, Texas. Win McNamee/Getty Images

Netanyahu’s opponents are watching, but with less alarm than before. “A year ago, our camp was calling anyone close to Trump to prevent an endorsement,” one senior opposition figure said. “Now it doesn’t really matter, the charm is not there.” Another opposition source said they had conveyed messages urging the White House to stay out of the race and appreciated that Trump has so far done so.

When Trump was asked specifically about who is currently polling as Netanyahu’s leading challenger, he said, “Well, I don’t know, I don’t hear bad things about him.” He then said, “They’ve written Bibi off many, many times, just like they’ve written me off many, many times. I wouldn’t underestimate Bibi.”

Trump has his own reasons for distance. American public opinion of Israel has fallen sharply, declining even more against the backdrop of the Iran war. Israel’s average net favorability fell from +51 points in July 2018 to -16 in July 2026, according to multiple polls, a 67-point drop over eight years.

As America quickly soured on the Iran war, a source familiar with the relationship said, Trump has been “trying to shed the image that Netanyahu pulled him into it.”

Still, the apparent distance may be misleading. Israeli sources say the two leaders have recently discussed renewed strikes on Iran. Israeli security sources told CNN preparations are underway – pending Trump’s decision – with timing unclear because of the US midterm elections.

Netanyahu rejected suggestions he was seeking escalation before the vote.

“It is not convenient for us, it’s no good,” he told Army Radio this week. He complained that if Iran fired missiles at Israel, his opponents “will blame me.”

World.title: Grand Egyptian Museum ticket prices to increase starting November 1
World.content:
Ticket prices for the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) will increase starting Sunday, November 1.

This adjustment applies to all visitor categories—including Egyptians, Arabs, and foreign nationals—as well as students, children, and senior citizens, depending on the specific ticket type.

Visitors are advised to check the specific rates applicable to their category before completing their booking.

New Ticket Prices

Egyptian visitors: The ticket price increases from LE 200 to LE 220.

The ticket price increases from LE 200 to LE 220. Egyptian students, children, and seniors: The ticket price increases from LE 100 to LE 110.

The ticket price increases from LE 100 to LE 110. Arab or foreign visitors: The ticket price increases from LE 1,570 to LE 1,830.

The ticket price increases from LE 1,570 to LE 1,830. Arab or foreign students and children: The ticket price increases from LE 790 to LE 920.

The ticket price increases from LE 790 to LE 920. Foreigners residing in Egypt: The ticket price increases from LE 790 to LE 920.

The ticket price increases from LE 790 to LE 920. Foreign students and children residing in Egypt: The ticket price increases from LE 400 to LE 460.

Online Booking

Those wishing to visit GEM can book their tickets online through the official website.

It is recommended to consult the official website prior to your visit to confirm the current prices and booking details.

Visiting Hours

According to the published schedule, the museum welcomes visitors as follows:

Sunday to Friday (excluding Saturdays and Wednesdays): The museum complex is open from 8:30 am to 7:00 pm.; exhibition halls are open from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm, with the final opportunity to purchase tickets at 5:00 pm.

World.title: Sisi proposes program to prepare candidates for Presidency
World.content:
Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi put forward a proposal to prepare and qualify potential future candidates for the presidency—specifically individuals holding doctoral degrees from prestigious Egyptian or foreign universities—through a 30-month training program at the Egyptian Military Academy.

During a graduation ceremony for new cohorts from the military colleges and the Egyptian Military Academy, on Saturday, Sisi said that the program would target individuals between the ages of 40-50 who meet the legal requirements for presidential candidacy.

The Military Academy would undertake the preparation and qualification of participants, enabling them to understand the nature of the Egyptian state, the mechanisms by which it is governed, and how to preserve it.

Sisi emphasized that the Academy would cover all costs of the program, regardless of the amount, Sky News Arabia, reported on Saturday.

Legislative framework

Sisi discussed the possibility of preparing groups of 200, 300, or 500 individuals, thereby providing citizens with a pool of qualified candidates from which to choose for the office of the President.

The president called upon the Speaker of Parliament to take charge of developing a legislative framework for this proposal in collaboration with a select group of trusted thinkers and politicians, and with the participation of the Ministries of Higher Education and Justice, with the ultimate goal of drafting a law to regulate the election of those who meet the established criteria.

He emphasized that the program’s objective is to prepare cadres capable of assuming the responsibilities of governance, understanding the requirements of state administration, and safeguarding the nation’s institutions.

‘No criminal, no traitor, shall ever govern Egypt after me’

Sisi stated: “No person with malicious intent, no criminal, and no traitor shall ever govern Egypt after me,” underscoring the importance of preserving the Egyptian state and its future.

Details regarding the mechanisms for selecting program participants, as well as how the proposed qualification process relates to existing constitutional and legal requirements for presidential candidacy, remain unclear.

This proposal emerges at a time when the Egyptian Constitution stipulates specific criteria for running for the presidency, including a minimum age of 40 and the requirement to secure parliamentary or public endorsement, in accordance with procedures set forth by law.

World.title: PM reviews economic reform agenda ahead of Egypt Forum 2026
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly on Saturday, October 17, 2026, reviewed the economic agenda for Egypt Forum 2026 and the country’s National Economic Transformation Program, aiming at building on previous reforms and strengthening sustainable and resilient growth.

Madbouly chaired a meeting attended by Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk and Planning and Economic Development Minister Ahmed Rostom to discuss the proposed economic sessions and working papers for the forum, which is being organized under President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s directives.

He said the sessions should present a comprehensive and transparent vision of the government’s future economic policies to citizens, the business community and the private sector, describing them as partners in production and development.

Discussions covered improving coordination between fiscal and monetary policies, expanding private-sector participation, enhancing the investment climate, and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises and entrepreneurship.

The meeting also reviewed plans to maximize returns from public assets and infrastructure, alongside targets through 2030 to improve healthcare, education and housing services and strengthen social protection.

World.title: Video: Egypt thrashes Saudi Arabia 5-0 in U-17 Gulf Cup
World.content:
Egypt’s national team secured a resounding 5-0 victory over Saudi Arabia during the Saturday evening match held as part of the U-17 Gulf Cup.

The two sides faced off at the Hamad Al-Kabir Stadium in Doha, in the opening round of the group stage of the U-17 Gulf Cup.

The Egyptian national team has now secured its first three points in Group B, which also includes Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Yemen, and Iraq.

Egypt is set to face Kuwait on October 20 as part of the second round of matches at the Hamad Al-Kabir Stadium in Doha, Qatar, at 5:45 PM.

World.title: Liberia: LAA Unveils $59 Million Modernization Plan Under Hughes’ Leadership
World.content:
Five-Year Strategy Targets Aviation Safety, Airport Security, Financial Reforms and Domestic Connectivity

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — The Liberia Airport Authority (LAA), under Managing Director Ernest Hughes, has outlined a five-year, US$59 million modernization plan aimed at addressing critical aviation safety gaps, improving airport services, strengthening financial management and expanding domestic connectivity.



The LAA Strategic Plan 2027–2031, themed “Modern Airports. Connected People. A Stronger Liberia,” positions Roberts International Airport (RIA) as the centerpiece of efforts to establish Liberia as a competitive aviation and logistics hub in West Africa.

The plan acknowledges longstanding challenges, including outdated navigation systems, inadequate emergency equipment, airport encroachment, weak financial controls and limited revenue diversification. It proposes measurable targets and institutional reforms, but implementation will depend on financing, procurement and sustained management oversight.

US$59 Million for Five Priorities

The strategy distributes its proposed investment across five areas:

US$18.5 million for aviation safety and navigation;

US$15 million for revenue diversification and cargo logistics;

US$12 million for airport security and perimeter protection;

US$9.5 million for passenger services; and

US$4 million for governance and enterprise resource planning.

The LAA proposes financing the program through a combination of public-private partnerships, development-bank financing, donor grants, government allocations and internally generated revenue.

The plan identifies more than US$8 million in European Union funding secured for safety, security and critical infrastructure improvements at RIA.

Its proposed financing model aims to reduce dependence on government appropriations, although the authority will need to secure commitments and demonstrate sound financial management to attract the necessary investment.

Safety Gaps Top the Agenda

The most urgent challenge identified in the plan is aviation safety and regulatory compliance.

The document cites a 2022 international aviation audit score of 27 percent, well below the global benchmark of 75 percent. It also identifies the destruction of the airport’s Doppler Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (DVOR) navigation system, the absence of a functional air traffic control voice-recording system and inadequate firefighting capacity.

According to the plan, RIA has two obsolete fire trucks, compared with four identified as necessary to meet applicable requirements. The loss of navigation infrastructure has also forced aviation personnel to rely on operational workarounds.

The proposed US$18.5 million safety allocation would fund replacement navigation equipment, a modern Instrument Landing System, upgraded air traffic control communications, runway safety improvements and modern fire and rescue apparatus.

The LAA is targeting international certification by the fourth quarter of 2027. That goal, however, depends on completing corrective measures and satisfying regulatory requirements.

The Liberia Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA) retains responsibility for certification decisions, while the LAA must provide and maintain the infrastructure and systems needed to meet applicable standards.

The division of responsibilities makes coordination between the airport operator and regulator essential as the deadline approaches.

Security and Perimeter Protection

The plan allocates US$12 million to strengthen airport security, including perimeter fencing, surveillance, signage and passenger and cargo screening.

It identifies illegal land occupation, community encroachment and informal settlements around RIA as potential vulnerabilities that could expose airport operations to unauthorized access, wildlife hazards and foreign object debris.

The authority also intends to work with communities and wildlife management specialists to reduce hazards around operational areas.

Delivering these improvements will require effective coordination with security agencies, careful procurement and progress in resolving land-related disputes.

Passenger Services and Cargo Development

Despite improvements to RIA’s passenger terminal, the strategic assessment identifies congestion, unreliable air conditioning, inefficient baggage handling and maintenance shortcomings.

The proposed US$9.5 million passenger-services investment would support digital check-in, improved passenger movement, upgraded commercial spaces and lounges, and digitized parking operations. The authority also plans to strengthen performance requirements for concessionaires and ground handlers.

Alongside these improvements, the LAA intends to develop RIA into a specialized cargo and logistics hub, using US$15 million to expand revenue-generating activities and cargo-handling capacity.

Proposed investments include temperature-controlled storage for agricultural products, seafood and other perishable exports. The strategy builds on the existing Roberts Air Cargo Center, operated through a public-private arrangement involving Global Logistics Services and National Aviation Services.

The plan argues that improved cold-chain facilities could reduce post-harvest losses and help Liberian producers reach overseas markets. However, success will also depend on reliable electricity, export certification, appropriate handling standards and coordination with producers and relevant government agencies.

The LAA projects that non-aeronautical revenue will increase from less than 15 percent of gross income to more than 45 percent by 2031. Achieving that target would reduce reliance on passenger traffic and aviation-related charges, but will require commercial investments that generate sustainable returns.

Financial Reform and Accountability

The plan identifies manual accounting, procurement delays, weak internal controls and limited performance monitoring as obstacles to institutional efficiency.

It states that the authority has completed a physical asset verification and established a fixed-asset register. It also reports that IFRS-compliant financial statements were produced in 2027 for the 2024 and 2025 financial years.

The next proposed step is an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system integrating finance, procurement, human resources and airport operations. The system is intended to strengthen reporting, reduce revenue leakages and improve expenditure controls.

Additional measures include a board-level governance, risk and compliance committee, a specialized legal and regulatory unit, stronger procurement safeguards and independent governance audits.

The LAA also proposes a Program Management Office to coordinate implementation and monitor performance. Under its results-based management framework, departmental heads would report quarterly against defined indicators, with corrective action required when targets are missed.

The LAA Strategic Plan 2027–2031, launched under Ernest Hughes’ leadership, themed “Modern Airports. Connected People. A Stronger Liberia,” positions RIA as the centerpiece of efforts to establish Liberia as a competitive aviation and logistics hub in West Africa.

Reviving Domestic Airports

These mechanisms could improve accountability, but their effectiveness will depend on reliable reporting and the authority’s willingness to address persistent underperformance.

Beyond RIA, the strategy proposes public-private partnerships and Build-Operate-Transfer arrangements to rehabilitate and operate five secondary airports: Harper, Greenville, Zwedru, Voinjama and Foya. Improvements would include runway and apron rehabilitation, terminal upgrades, perimeter fencing and safety equipment.

Foya receives particular attention because of its proximity to Guinea and Sierra Leone and its potential connection to the Mano River Union Hub.

To attract investors despite limited traffic, the plan proposes viability-gap funding to help cover initial financing and commercial challenges. It also outlines revenue-sharing arrangements under which private operators would retain a larger share of aeronautical revenue in the early years before progressively sharing non-aeronautical surpluses with the state.

The strategy further envisages requiring a selected private operator to establish and operate a domestic and regional airline.

Such a model could improve connections between Monrovia and other parts of Liberia, but it raises questions about route profitability, public financial exposure and the capacity to enforce concession terms. Transparent procurement, rigorous due diligence and clear performance obligations will be critical to protecting public assets.

Workforce and Energy Modernization

The plan recognizes that infrastructure investment must be matched by a technically capable workforce.

Training priorities include aviation security, fire and rescue, safety management, engineering maintenance and technical services aligned with International Civil Aviation Organization and International Air Transport Association requirements. A proposed Human Resource Information System would help track staff qualifications and recurrent training.

The authority also plans to modernize internal electrical distribution systems and explore solar and other renewable energy solutions. Reliable power is essential for navigation equipment, screening systems and terminal operations, while reduced dependence on diesel generators could improve resilience and lower operating costs.

Hughes’ Implementation Challenge

Despite its wide-ranging ambitions, the plan acknowledges significant constraints, including limited departmental budgets, staffing shortages, outdated equipment and uncertainty over sustained financing.

An internal assessment cited in the document gave confidence in the LAA’s ability to become a leading West African aviation hub within five years an average score of 4.88 out of 10. Only 29.4 percent of respondents expressed high confidence in that prospect. Departmental budget adequacy scored 2.5 out of five, while confidence in readiness for an unannounced aviation regulatory audit scored 2.8.

The findings underline the gap between the authority’s ambitions and its current capacity.

For Hughes and his management team, early tests will include restoring critical navigation systems, improving firefighting capacity, strengthening perimeter security, maintaining credible financial records and demonstrating measurable progress toward certification.

The authority must also ensure that public-private partnerships are competitively awarded, financially viable and structured to protect the government’s long-term interests.

The LAA’s proposed US$59 million program is distinct from the broader US$250 million aviation-sector investment projected under the civil aviation master plan; the figures represent different levels of planned investment.

If implemented effectively, the strategy could improve safety, expand domestic connectivity, support agricultural exports and give the authority a more sustainable revenue base. But those gains will depend on financing, execution and accountability—not the plan alone.

For Hughes, the central challenge is to turn the five-year roadmap into demonstrable results: safer airports, more reliable services and a financially stronger LAA.

World.title: Curated Cultural Gifts Expands to Roberts International Airport
World.content:
Monrovia, Liberia – Curated Cultural Gifts, a Liberian-owned business founded by entrepreneur Brenda Brewer Moore, has expanded its operations with the opening of a new kiosk at Roberts International Airport (RIA), located in the Departure Hall.

Established in 2021, Curated Cultural Gifts was founded with a mission to showcase African arts and crafts, celebrate cultural heritage, and provide meaningful gifts that reflect Liberia’s rich history, creativity, and traditions.

The business currently operates a store on Old Road in Monrovia and is preparing to open another location at Kpatawee Waterfalls in Bong County.



According to founder Brenda Brewer Moore, the airport expansion represents an important opportunity to introduce Liberian and African craftsmanship to an international audience.

“Although the kiosk is a small space, we see it as a big opportunity to share our culture with the world. Our goal is to promote Liberia positively through arts and crafts while creating greater visibility and economic opportunities for local artisans,” Moore said.

Curated Cultural Gifts is also inviting talented Liberian and African artisans to submit their products for consideration as the business expands its collection of culturally inspired gifts and souvenirs.

Moore expressed appreciation to customers, partners, and supporters who have contributed to the business’s growth over the past five years.

“Every purchase, referral, and word of encouragement has helped us reach this point. We are grateful and excited about what lies ahead,” she added.

Curated Cultural Gifts continues to position itself as a destination for authentic African crafts, meaningful cultural gifts, and products that celebrate Liberia’s heritage.

World.title: Liberia: U.S. Trial of Former Army Commander Moses Wright, Linked to Lutheran Church Massacre, Postponed Until February
World.content:
U.S. Homeland security agents arrest Moses Slanger Wright at his home in Philadelphia in 2022.

Summary:

The trial of Moses Wright, 73, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of lying to immigration agents about his involvement in Liberia’s civil conflict has been postponed to February. It was set to start in November. The court has yet to give a reason for the delay.

U.S. prosecutors allege that Wright concealed his involvement in wartime atrocities when seeking immigration benefits and citizenship. He faces immigration-related charges, because the U.S. did not have laws in place to try citizens for war crimes committed in international jurisdictions when the alleged crimes took place.

Wright faces a maximum possible sentence of 165 years in prison and a US$7 million fine.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

The U.S. trial of Moses Wright, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of ordering and overseeing the 1990 St. Peter’s Lutheran Church massacre in which an estimated 600 men, women and children were killed, has been postponed again.



Wright’s trial, previously scheduled for November in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, has been rescheduled for February, the latest in a series of delays.

“We see it as a setback to our quest for justice,” said Marcus P. Quoigoah, executive director of the Lutheran Massacre Survivors Association, in a phone interview. “We are frustrated. Looking at the lives of so many that have been shattered as a result of Wright and his men, delaying this, we feel that justice is still being halted.”

The postponement comes more than 36 years after the massacre, for which no one has been criminally convicted in Liberia. It also comes as legislation to establish a War and Economic Crimes Court has stalled at the Liberian Legislature, while survivors continue to pursue accountability through legal proceedings abroad.

Wright, 73, faces federal immigration fraud and perjury charges over allegations that he concealed his involvement in atrocities during Liberia’s first civil war to obtain immigration benefits and eventually U.S. citizenship.

According to a June 2022 indictment announced by the U.S. Department of Justice , Wright allegedly committed atrocities against civilians or ordered troops under his command to carry them out, including the persecution of members of the Gio and Mano ethnic groups, murder, assault, unlawful arrests and imprisonment.

Wright is believed to be a cousin of the late President Samuel Doe, and his alleged role during the First Liberian Civil War was General Commander of the Armed Forces of Liberia, which would make him one of the most prominent figures in the conflict. Liberia’s 2009 Truth and Reconciliation Commission report also named Wright, Moses Thomas, James Chelly and George Dweh in the June 1990 massacre of 27 Gio and Mano family members of Armed Forces of Liberia personnel living at the Barclay Training Center barracks in Monrovia. The killings were carried out “reportedly under orders of Samuel Doe,” according to the report. The commission also implicated Chelly, an army captain, in military operations against civilians in Nimba County, stating that he and Edwin Voker “commanded the onslaught.”

Dweh, a senior figure in the Movement for Democracy in Liberia, rebel group who became Speaker of Liberia’s transitional legislature in 2003, died in April 2020 without facing prosecution for his alleged involvement in the massacre or other wartime abuses.

The massacre occurred in July 1990, when soldiers of the Armed Forces of Liberia attacked civilians sheltering at St. Peter’s Lutheran Church in Monrovia during the country’s first civil war. Although it is not explicitly mentioned in Wright’s indictment, he commanded the army when the massacre took place. He oversaw Moses Thomas, a more junior commander, who was found civilly liable for the massacre in a 2021 case. The court ordered him to pay $84 million in damages to four survivors and relatives of victims. He fled the United States for Liberia avoiding enforcement of the fine.

“We still hold him responsible for the over 600 lives that were murdered,” said Quoigoah. “Wright had a hand; he had a big stake in it.”

Prosecutors say Wright obtained asylum in the United States in 2000, permanent residency in 2008 and applied for citizenship in 2013. He allegedly concealed his wartime conduct during the immigration process and repeated false statements under oath during an August 2016 naturalization interview.

Wright is not being prosecuted directly for violations of international law including war crimes or crimes against humanity because of limitations in U.S. federal law. The United States enacted so-called “universal jurisdiction” laws that allow government to prosecute people for crimes committed outside the country, after the alleged atrocities in Liberia in 1990. Those laws cannot be applied retroactively to conduct that occurred before they took effect.

Instead, prosecutors have brought immigration fraud and perjury charges, an approach previously used against other Liberian war criminals, including Mohammed Jabateh and Thomas Woewiyu, who were convicted in Philadelphia in 2017 and 2018, respectively. Jabateh is serving a 30-year sentence. Woewiyu died while awaiting sentencing. In 2026 former Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy commander Layee Sekou Camara, known as during the war as “K1,” pleaded guilty after being charged with immigration offenses. He is serving a nearly five-year sentence.

Other former Liberian rebel commanders have also been deported from the United States over immigration violations linked to their wartime activities. They include George Boley, former leader of the Liberia Peace Council, who was deported in March 2012 after a U.S. immigration court found that he had engaged in extrajudicial killings and recruited and used child soldiers. Mayama Sesay, known as “Black Diamond,” a former commander of the Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy rebel group, was deported in September 2025 after an immigration judge found that she had lied about recruiting and using child soldiers during her immigration applications.

Wright has denied the charges. If convicted on all counts, he faces a maximum sentence of 165 years in prison and $7 million in fines.

The proceedings against Wright have been accompanied by security concerns involving Liberian investigators. In September, the Global Justice and Research Project, a leading Liberian war crimes investigation organization, relocated a senior investigator following repeated death threats allegedly linked to Wright’s sympathizers .

Among the survivors still seeking accountability is Rufus Kartee, 65, who says a bullet struck his left hip during the massacre, damaging the bone and leaving him dependent on a crutch for more than three decades.

A mass grave inside the compound of St. Peter’s Lutheran Church in Monrovia, where an estimated 600 people were massacred in July 1990.Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Kartee spoke to FrontPage Africa/New Narratives before undergoing surgery at the John F. Kennedy Memorial Medical Center in Monrovia this month. He said he hoped to see those responsible brought to justice before more survivors died.

“The main, main people them dying on a daily basis,” he said. “Even people from our side too are dying on a daily basis.”

Kartee said seeing alleged perpetrators face trial remains a priority.

“So, we that are alive today, if I will survive, I will still be happy to see the people going through court process.”

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. Funding was provided by the U.N. Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and the European Union. The funders had no say in the story’s content.
