World.title: Shipping attacks threaten Turkey's resolve to keep warships out of Black Sea
World.content:
A wave of deadly attacks on cargo ships in the waters of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania has jolted the alliance into calling an emergency meeting on Black Sea security. Yet any move to send NATO ships hinges on Turkey reversing its steadfast refusal to allow warships into the Black Sea.

Advertising

Thursday saw two chemical tankers struck by drones close to a Romanian port.

It follows two similar attacks in Bulgarian waters in the past week. More than 20 sailors have been killed or remain missing.

“The war has come in full force to the Black Sea now,” said Yoruk Isik, a maritime analyst who runs the Istanbul-based Bosphorus Observer consultancy. “With the change in technology compared to the beginning of the war, drones really disrupted maritime traffic.”

According to Isik, the latest attacks underscore the growing spread of the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. “Russian ports and Ukrainian ports are heavily targeted, but now even in NATO waters ships are getting hit, in Bulgarian waters, Romanian waters.

“We are at a point where there is no safe place.”

The latest strikes targeted vessels along a key Ukrainian shipping route, casting Russia as NATO’s prime suspect as Moscow intensifies its assault on Ukrainian trade.

After meeting on Thursday with the leaders of Bulgaria and Romania, both NATO members, Secretary-General Mark Rutte said the military alliance would “continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed”.

Romanian President Nicușor Dan said NATO would hold a crisis meeting next week to discuss the situation.

Gatekeeper to the Black Sea

NATO could deploy air defence systems against drones to protect Bulgarian and Romanian waters.

But any deployment of naval ships will depend on NATO member Turkey, which controls access to the Black Sea through the Turkish Straits under a long-standing international treaty, the 1936 Montreux Convention.

Since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, Ankara has blocked entry of Russian and Ukrainian warships or military vessels belonging to NATO members without a Black Sea coast, arguing for a diplomatic solution.

In recent weeks the Turkish government has sought to broker a ceasefire on commercial shipping, without success. Isik claims that failure, coupled with the latest escalation in attacks, is increasingly calling into question Ankara’s reliance on diplomacy alone.

“Either they’re going to have a breakthrough and the Kremlin is going to de-escalate, or Ankara is going to accept the reality that there needs to be a more credible force here – bigger vessels have to come,” the analyst said.

He pointed out that the navies of Romania and Bulgaria are not equipped to handle such an operation alone, with Cold War-era ships nearing the end of their lifespan.

“So Turkey's engagement is key to any successful NATO planning in the Black Sea.”

Russian leverage

Despite Turkish-owned cargo ships coming under attack in recent weeks, and Turkey’s deep reliance on Black Sea trade, Ankara has so far kept its powerful navy on the sidelines.

International relations expert Huseyin Bagci, of Ankara’s Middle East Technical University, says Turkey fears an escalation in the conflict and will be wary of allowing NATO ships into the Black Sea.

“I do not think the government would dare,” said Bagci. “Probably the government considers this a provocation to drag Turkey into the war... Turkey is afraid of getting involved in the Black Sea against Russia, this is somehow a trauma in the Turkish mind.”

Moscow also retains powerful leverage over Ankara, he suggested.

Russia’s state nuclear company Rosatom is about to complete a multi-billion-dollar nuclear power station in Akkuyu, southern Turkey. Ankara sees it as vital to the drive to reduce its heavy dependence on imported energy. “It is illogical to oppose Russia now while you let the Russians complete the nuclear plant,” said Bagci.

Erdogan hints at larger nuclear partnership with Russia, unsettling Turkey's allies

Ankara also knows that letting NATO vessels in while barring Russian warships could provoke Moscow into contesting Turkey’s prized status as the gatekeeper to the Black Sea.

However, retired Turkish diplomat Selim Kuneralp, an expert on the Montreux Convention, warns Turkey’s control over Black Sea access is likely already in Russian President Vladimir Putin’s sights.

“This has probably had an impact on Russia’s ability to conduct the war, and I doubt that Putin is very happy with the situation,” said Kuneralp. “So if he were to win the war, there is a very strong risk that he will take the initiative of saying: ‘this is unacceptable and we want to have free passage of warships from now on, regardless of whether there is a war’.”

As a signatory, Moscow has the right to call for a revision of the Montreux Convention every five years.

For centuries, Russia fought repeated wars with the then Ottoman Empire for control of the Turkish Straits. In the early years of the Cold War, even Joseph Stalin tried his hand, but the United States intervened and thwarted him.

Now Ankara walks a tightrope between Moscow and its NATO partners to avoid a resurrection of those historical rivalries.

World.title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waivers, accuses Zelenskyy of 'prolonging war'
World.content:
US President Donald Trump again accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. The remarks come amid renewed tensions over US policy toward Moscow including waiving some sanctions.

US President Donald Trump on Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war.

"My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"Zelenskyy doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," he added.

Trump signed an executive order late Friday waiving broad new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine's defense.

He has also temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing supplies to flow into global markets in a bid to lower fuel prices ahead of US midterm elections on November 3.

Trump links Russia sanctions waiver to fuel prices ahead of midterms

Opinion polls suggest that Republicans could face significant losses in the election, as voters voice growing frustration over fuel prices that have surged since the Iran war began in late February.

Most economists believe the suspension of congressionally approved sanctions on Russia and the diesel deal with the Kremlin will do little to lower US fuel prices.

Trump also repeated his claim that Ukraine was targeting Russian refineries to hurt Republicans ahead of the midterm election.

How Trump is helping Putin To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The move drew a sharp response from Kyiv and its allies, further straining relations between Trump and Zelenskyy.

Zelenskyy warns Ukraine cannot prevail if US backs Russia

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Sunday that Ukraine would lose its defensive battle against Russia if the United States switched sides and supported Moscow.

"If the United States will take the side of Russia, of course we will not prevail," Zelenskyy told NBC's 'Meet the Press' calling a withdrawal of US support "a historic mistake and big tragedy."

He said Washington had resumed sharing intelligence after it was "blocked for some period of time," adding that Ukraine had missed critical intelligence on ballistic missile attacks for three days.

Zelenskyy also criticized US restrictions affecting Ukraine's war effort, saying, "We are strategic partners," but "we cannot applaud when someone turns against Ukraine."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump's suspension of new sanctions on Russia, saying Trump wanted to assess their impact on the global and US economies.

Zelenskyy speaks to US envoys as Trump renews criticism

Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke to US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as Russia and Ukraine attacked each other's energy infrastructure, leaving thousands without power in Ukraine and setting an oil refinery ablaze near Saint Petersburg.

After the talks, Zelenskyy said "a lot depends" on the US position, adding that "this war must be brought to an end." Ukraine was ready to work "constructively" and "honestly," he said, calling for the same approach from its European and US partners.

Zelenskyy said he also discussed deliveries of US Patriot air defense systems as Kyiv struggles to counter Russian missiles.

A US-led push to end the war has yet to yield a breakthrough, with Trump expressing frustration at both Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Zelenskyy accused Moscow of violating Trump's "energy ceasefire" 76 times and warned Russia planned to deprive Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter. Russian strikes left "tens of thousands" without power, he said, while Ukrainian officials reported three deaths.

Ukraine launched drones at Putin's hometown of Saint Petersburg late Sunday, setting an oil refinery ablaze and killing one person, Moscow said.

Edited by: Dmytro Hubenko

World.title: Canada: Fire at Alberta military Base kills four, leaves 19 in critical condition
World.content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says a "serious incident" sparked a major fire at on Alberta military base. Four people have died, 39 are in hospital and at least 19 are in critical condition.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said on Sunday that 39 people were in the hospital after a fire at a Canadian military base killed four people. At least 19 were in critical condition.

The fire broke out at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of Canada's busiest military training bases, at about 4 p.m. local time (2200 GMT) Saturday.

Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division, said the army responded to a "serious fire incident" during a training exercise conducted by the Third Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.

A grass fire ignited in the training area during the exercise, Rutland said at a news conference Sunday, adding that the cause was under investigation.

"What I would say is there was multiple training activities happening throughout the training area at the time," he said, adding that "uncommonly strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly and shift direction towards the range administrative area."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Saturday called the incident one of the worst tragedies the army has suffered in peace time.

"It is with deep sadness that I can confirm, at this time, that four service members have lost their lives and that their loved ones have been notified," Carney said in the capital Ottawa, adding that "dozens of others have been seriously injured."

"We will care for the injured through every step of their recovery," Carney said.

"And we will stand by the women and men of our armed forces as they bear the weight of this loss, they will not carry it alone because in Canada we take care of one another."

Medical facilities around base 'overwhelmed'

A doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, which is located some 180 kilometers (120 miles) northwest of the base, told national broadcaster CBC that people were being brought to hospitals across the city.

Dr. Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, said health-care facilities around the base itself had been "completely overwhelmed" by the number of people requiring medical aid.

"This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton," he said. "It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster."

The injured were brought to Wainwright Health Center Image: John Ulan/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/picture alliance

What else do we know about the major fire in Alberta?

The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was spreading rapidly due to high winds.

"The fire south of Wainwright crossed the base fence earlier today and is being actively managed ... Emergency crews remain focused on protecting life safety, homes, and other structures," it said.



The incident occurred just days before people in Alberta, home to the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, will vote in the October 19 referendum on whether the province wants to begin the process of separating from the rest of Canada.

World.title: Ebola: Kenya cases rise to 8, spreads to 8th Congo province
World.content:
A senior health official in Kenya said there have now been 8 Ebola infections in the country, while in DR Congo the disease has spread to an eighth province.

Kenya's Health Ministry on Sunday confirmed another case of Ebola, bringing the number of confirmed infections in the country to eight.

News of another patient in the East African state came as health officials in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported that the outbreak there had spread to an eighth province.

What Kenya's health director general said

"Today, 38 people were tested, and one tested positive for Ebola," Health Ministry Director-General Dr. Patrick Amoth said in an ​interview on Kenya's Citizen TV.

"He is a 49-year-old man ​who is not a healthcare worker. He developed ​fever, headache and muscle pain," Amoth said.

He went on to explain that the latest case was a patient attendant who cleaned utensils and linen and had likely been exposed to Kenya's first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month.

Amoth said patients in quarantine were being tested after developing symptoms and that the other six patients were stable after receiving supportive treatment. The first patient died on October 5.

Kenya has been on a heightened state of alert as a major outbreak of the highly contagious disease spread in Congo in central Africa.

Ebola now in 8th province in Congo

Also on Sunday, authorities in DRC said that the Ebola outbreak had spread to an eighth province in the north.

Congo's Health Ministry said that two cases including a death were recorded in Nord-Ubangi province which borders the Central African Republic (CAR).

"We see pockets of Ebola generally going down, but unfortunately geographically it's spreading out," said World Health Organization Regional Director for Africa Mohamed Yakub Janabi in an interview with The Associated Press in Beni, eastern Congo, on Friday.

It's currently the deadliest outbreak in Congo's history with authorities recording at least 9,400 cases, including over 4,500 deaths, in the outbreak declared in mid-May.

The current epidemic is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare type of Ebola that has no approved vaccine or treatment.

Ebola is spread between people by direct contact with bodily fluids. It can cause fever, fatigue, and muscle pain, followed by vomiting and diarrhea. Some patients also develop internal or external bleeding.

World.title: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama ignores calls to resign amid violent clashes
World.content:
Anti-government protesters continued calls for Edi Rama to step down as violent clashes between demonstrators and police again took place.

Student-led protests continued in Albania for a sixth day with continued demands for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

Despite those calls, Rama is refusing to step down, saying the demonstrations were not a threat to government but rather a threat to Albania's ambition of accession to the European Union.

Protesters gathered again at noon in front of the education ministry chanting "Rama, resign" amid a tense standoff with police Image: Hameraldi Agolli/AP Photo/picture alliance

What Rama said

"I ​am not being challenged, the government is not being challenged, a government majority or a winning party in the elections is not being challenged but a path is being challenged, a mission is being challenged," Rama said in a live address on Facebook.

"Albanians need to think ​very clearly: Do they want this, do they want that, or do they want the EU?” Rama asked.

Rama ruled out resigning and said that the protests are the "work of an outside hand."

Earlier in the week Rama ruled out resigning, saying that governments were changed through elections.

Student-led demonstrations, spurred by discontent over alleged government corruption, unemployment and poor education standards, have rocked central Tirana and spread to other cities in the past week.

Riot police use water cannon and rubber bullets after demonstrators threw Molotov cocktails and threw rocks and fireworks Image: Boris Grdanoski/AP Photo/picture alliance

Continued clashes between protesters and police

On Sunday, hundreds gathered outside the Education Ministry, chanting "Rama resign!" and threw rocks ​at riot police who responded with tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets.

The protests come at a difficult for Albania as it is among a group of Balkan states seeking to join the EU by 2030.

There have been calls for calm from Brussels amid the violent protests. The European Commission in Sunday condemned the use of ⁠violence ⁠in Tirana and othern cities.

The commission added that it welcomed the Albanian authorities' ​commitment that the right to protest will ​be protected.

World.title: Israel: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of elections
World.content:
The US president said he supports Israel's current prime minister in the country's elections on October 27. But polls say Netanyahu and his far-right partners currently lack the majority to secure a new term.

US President Donald Trump has announced his "complete and total" endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Israel will hold parliamentary elections on October 27, with opinion polls suggesting neither Netanyahu nor the opposition will manage to secure the 61 seats needed to form a coalition.

"Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu," Trump posted on his Truth Social account.

Iran war at center of Trump announcement

According to Trump, Netanyahu is a "Great Warrior Prime Minister," also commending him for his role in the war against Iran.

"BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!" Trump added.

Netanyahu thanked the US leader for his "tremendous support."

"Together we will complete the mission," Netanyahu posted on his X account, alluding to the joint campaign by the two countries against Iran.

Netanyahu has been vocal in his objection to Iran's nuclear program Image: Richard Drew/AP Photo/picture alliance

Trump said the US would be alone in the war against Iran if Netanyahu were not re-elected, also mentioning the chant often sung at events by Iran's Revolutionary Guards that calls for both the US' and Israel's death, also labeling the two countries "the big and small Satans."

"If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," Trump said.

Netanyahu opponent reacts

The war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February and resulted in Tehran blocking some global oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger, reacted to Trump's endorsement by saying the Israeli public are the only ones who decide who is the country's next leader.

Speaking at an event in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot voiced his appreciation of Trump's "large contribution" to Israel's security.

"But Israel is a democratic state," he said, adding that the US administration will learn to work with whichever government the public decides on.

Netanyahu boasts Trump friendship once again

This is not the first time Netanyahu's election campaign has invoked Trump's support to augment the Israeli leader's international status.

In 2019, Netanyahu's Likud party posted billboards showing the Israeli leader shaking hands with Trump during the latter's first term as US president, as well as with Russian President Vladimir Putin, describing Netanyahu as a leader of a "different league."

Netanyahu is the longest serving prime minister in Israel's history. Much of Israeli society is divided on his far-right coalition's role in the failure to foresee and prevent the October 7 terrorist attack by Islamist Palestinian group Hamasand its affiliates in Gaza, in which some 1,200 Israelis were killed.

Netanyahu has refused to establish a state inquiry with the authority to look into government documents and summon ministers and officials to testify. Instead, the prime minister wants a commission with less authority to see confidential documents and with no authority to force testimonies by the country's leading politicians and officials.

Israeli opposition have been protesting against Benjamin Netanyahu's "failure" to prevent the October 7 attacks Image: Aviv Atlas/REUTERS

Another point of contention is Israel's war in Gaza that followed the attack, in which some 74,000 Palestinians have been killed.

Despite repeatedly promising a "total victory" after the war began, opposition supporters believe Netanyahu failed to deliver, with Hamas still in charge of many parts of the Gaza Strip. Netanyahu and his coalition partners have also promised to support what they called the "wilful migration" of Gaza residents, while also deepening Israel's hold on its territories in the West Bank, which is largely considered illegal under international law.

Other issues at the center of Israel's elections are the conscription of young ultraorthodox men into the military, the cost of living, and Israel's international status.

World.title: Saudi Arabia sends skyscraper employees home amid Houthi threats
World.content:
Riyadh's Kingdom Center tower's management told the people employed there to work from home "until further notice," without giving a reason. This comes as Houthi attacks escalate.

The Kingdom Center skyscraper in Riyadh told people employed there to work from home due to possible attacks by Yemen's Houthirebels.

The 99-storey tower is one of Saudi Arabia's tallest buildings.

Kingdom Center made working from home "mandatory" with no reason given. The new order is effective immediately and will be in power until further notice, the building's management told tenants, AFP reported.

Among the building's tenants are important financial institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, as well as wealth management company Merril Lynch.

At the building's foot is a shopping center, which will remain open for now.

Attacks increase

Studies in schools across Saudi capital Riyadh and the surrounding areas will take place online for a second week, with the city's King Khalid International Airport still being closed after a Houthi attack resulted in 13 casualties.

The conflict between the Saudi-led coalition and Iran-backed Islamist group Houthis has continued to escalate, with the coalition reporting its first military deaths since the escalation's beginning.

Two helicopter pilots were killed near the Yemen border due to a "technical malfunction," the coalition said, with the Houthis earlier announcing the downing of an Apache helicopter "belonging to the Saudi enemy," the group said.

The Houthis have carried out attacks on international airports in Saudi Arabia Image: Social Media/REUTERS

Conflict flares up again

On the Saudi side, two drones were intercepted over Riyadh overnight, with a third being shot down over the country's Eastern Province, a known oil-rich area, according to the authorities in the country.

Two ballistic missiles were also intercepted in Saudi Arabia's south.

The two sides have been confronting each other on various intensities over the past decade. After a four-year ceasefire, the conflict between the two sides saw an escalation after the Yemen-based Islamist militia took over strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthis have targeted oil facilities, tankers and Riyadh's international airport, with the coalition carrying out strikes on Houthi areas.

World.title: Meloni backs police after cost-of-living protests turn violent in Italian cities
World.content:
Anger over living costs and low wages has brought Italians onto the streets. A major union has called a general strike for November 20.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Sunday condemned rioting during cost-of-living protests, expressing solidarity with police after clashes in several cities.

The violence broke out during cost-of-living demonstrations on Saturday, leaving at least four police officers and 20 demonstrators injured in Milan.

The unrest comes amid anger over high prices, stagnant real wages and a shortage of affordable housing in major cities.

What happened during the protests?

In Milan, black-clad, masked youths threw fireworks and bottles at police and erected barricades in the central Piazza Duomo, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

Police initially withdrew to await reinforcements and later used tear gas to clear the square. Some 50 young people were arrested, about half of them minors, according to ANSA.

Clashes also broke out in Turin, Bologna and Bergamo. Police in Bologna used water cannon and made four arrests, all minors, with seven people reported to prosecutors.

How did Italy's PM Meloni respond?

Meloni expressed solidarity with police on Sunday, condemning criminals who she said exploited demonstrations to provoke confrontations and "sow chaos."

Italy tightens restrictions on the right to protest To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Demonstrating is a right, but setting our cities on fire is not," she said.

Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also condemned the violence while acknowledging the grievances behind the demonstrations.

"The reasons for the protest were understandable. The violence against police and the serious damage to the city, however, cannot be justified," he said.

Why were people demonstrating?

Protesters rallied against high living costs and low wages, with households facing expensive fuel and difficulty finding affordable housing.

In Rome, thousands joined a demonstration organized by the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL). Its leader, Maurizio Landini, announced a general strike for November 20.

The violence came as similar demonstrations in France descended into rioting, arson and looting, with more than 1,800 people arrested nationwide.

World.title: Ukraine apologizes after a suspected drone crashes in Lithuania, damaging a moving car.
World.content:
Debris has damaged a moving car in Lithuania, where NATO jets were scrambled. Kyiv says Russian jamming may have diverted drones targeting Russia.

Ukraine apologized Sunday after a suspected drone crashed in northern Lithuania, prompting shelter warnings and the deployment of NATO fighter jets.

The incident raised fresh concerns about the spillover of Russia's war against Ukraine into NATO territory, although the drone's origin and whether it carried explosives remained under investigation.

What happened in Lithuania?

Lithuanian authorities told residents in central and northern regions to seek shelter Sunday morning after detecting an unidentified flying object.

Debris damaged a moving civilian vehicle, but no one was injured, national crisis management centre chief Vilmantas Vitkauskas told Lithuanian radio.

Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said the drone probably entered from neighboring Poland. He proposed a joint investigation with Warsaw.

Lithuanian PM warns of Russian nuclear threat To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Two Italian Eurofighter jets operating under NATO command were deployed, a NATO spokesperson said. Kaunas said weather conditions prevented visual identification.

Have similar incidents happened before?

Lithuania and its Baltic neighbors have experienced several drone incursions during the war.

Ukrainian drones intended to strike targets in northwestern Russia have previously strayed into Baltic airspace and crashed. Russian-made drones have also entered Lithuania from Belarus.

Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda described Sunday's incident as another example of the war spilling onto NATO's eastern flank.

Meanwhile, Lithuania said it was treating an attempted arson attack on a Starlink base station near Vilnius as Russia-linked sabotage aimed at undermining Ukraine's military capacity.

National crisis management chief Vilmantas Vitkauskas said Sunday that authorities were searching for suspects who tried to set fire to the facility at about 2 a.m. (2300 GMT Saturday).

World.title: Macron acusa a la “extrema izquierda” de inflamar la calle
World.content:
Macron, en su discurso: ¿Cómo es posible que haya franceses que le hagan esto a Francia?

El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

El presidente francés desvincula a los estudiantes de la violencia y el vandalismo, pero asegura que “quienes hayan intentado derribar la República tendrán que responder por sus actos”

El presidente de la República francesa, Emmanuel Macron, compareció este domingo por la noche, después de varias semanas de disturbios, manifestaciones y protestas en la calle y un sábado especialmente dramático para el país. “Me dirijo a ustedes esta noche en un momento de extrema gravedad”, comenzó. “Unos alborotadores procedentes de grupos de extrema izquierda, a los que se sumaron numerosos delincuentes, saquearon comercios y destruyeron edificios públicos. ¿Por qué quemar el Ayuntamiento de Limoges? ¿Cómo pueden llegar a semejante extremo? Nada lo explica, nada lo justifica. Todos sentimos rabia y vergüenza”, afirmó sin concretar ninguna medida y apelando, sustancialmente, al paso del tiempo. “Faltan seis meses para las elecciones”.

El jefe del Estado, que anunció la creación de un gabinete de crisis para monitorizar la previsible violencia de los próximos días, admitió que la violencia sufrida había sido “inaudita” y acusó a grupúsculos de “extrema izquierda” apoyados por “numerosos delincuentes”. “He pedido al Gobierno que extraiga todas las lecciones necesarias en materia de inteligencia, y se hará con plena transparencia. Las investigaciones se llevarán a cabo con la máxima (…) firmeza”, explicó. “Nuestros jueces imparten justicia en vuestro nombre y saben lo que esperáis de ellos. Quienes hayan destruido deberán pagar por ello; quienes hayan intentado derribar la República tendrán que responder por sus actos”.

La jornada de manifestaciones y violencia del sábado dejó un balance de 2.000 detenidos, 855 de ellos solo en París. Hay 600 policías heridos y 1.500 comercios saqueados o destrozados. Macron también lamentó no haber tenido mejor información de lo que podía ocurrir y exigió explicaciones sobre los fallos de los servicios de inteligencia. Una afirmación que invita a pensar en ceses inminentes en ese departamento de la administración pública.

El presidente, a quienes muchos había reclamado en las últimas horas que declarara “el estado de urgencia”, anuncio que se prohibirán determinadas concentraciones en los próximos días. Pero pidió calma y recordó que hay elecciones en seis meses. No hay necesidad de agitar la calle, insistió sin tener una sola palabra hacia los estudiantes mutilados por los artefactos explosivos de la policía. Y, como el resto de fuerzas políticas, señaló directamente a La Francia Insumisa de Jean-Luc Mélenchon por, supuestamente, alentar a la revuelta. “Todos aquellos que hoy explican que la urgencia es salir a la calle solo persiguen un objetivo: secuestrar el debate. Los debates no deben desarrollarse en la calle ni mediante la violencia. Deben tener lugar con respeto, nunca en medio del desorden y los destrozos. Nuestro país merece unas elecciones presidenciales ejemplares dentro de seis meses”.

Macron quiso también separar a los agitadores de los estudiantes. “Jamás debemos confundir a los manifestantes que tienen reivindicaciones legítimas con aquellos que han destruido, destrozado y saqueado”, insistió. “Nuestra juventud siente una profunda angustia (…) ante su futuro y su capacidad para encontrar su lugar en la sociedad. Comprendo a nuestros alumnos de secundaria y a nuestros estudiantes universitarios, y ellos ocupan un lugar central en mi compromiso con la vida pública. Su voz debe ser escuchada. Nuestra responsabilidad es doble: escuchar la indignación y hacer respetar con firmeza el orden republicano”.

Los destrozos recorrieron todo el país el sábado. Un grupo de agitadores entró y vandalizó una comisaría y ocupó luego la entrada del Ayuntamiento de Marsella, forzando la puerta. El alcalde se vio obligado a pedir refuerzos personalmente a Macron. Lo mismo ocurrió en otras ciudades como Lille o Rennes.. O en Lyon, donde las llamas consumieron la oficina de turismo: “Es un drama”, lamentó su alcalde, Grégory Doucet. La imagen más espectacular y devastadora fue la del Ayuntamiento de Limoges (130.000 habitantes) ardiendo completamente y derrumbándose.

La violencia, lejos de detenerse, volvió a las calles el domingo. A solo dos horas de que empezara la reunión de crisis presidida por el jefe del Estado, Emmanuel Macron, las calles adyacentes a la plaza de la República volvieron a ser el escenario de carreras, lanzamiento de proyectiles y pillajes en tiendas. Un tipo de violencia más parecido al que se observa cuando hay una victoria del PSG o de la selección francesa que la que dejaron las protestas de los estudiantes durante la semana anterior.

World.title: Los disturbios vuelven al centro de París un día después de la gran revuelta
World.content:
La policía y varios grupos de agitadores se enfrentan en los alrededores de la plaza de la República entre barricadas, fuego y gases lacrimógenos

La vida parisina no se detuvo tras los salvajes disturbios del 17 de octubre en toda Francia. No lo hicieron, sobre todo, sus ciudadanos, que el domingo por la mañana salieron a comprar el desayuno esquivando bicicletas quemadas, contenedores y a algún runner. La mañana transcurrió en un ambiente de desolación y olor a plástico quemado y algunos descubrieron que su vehículo había sido calcinado. Pero pasadas las tres de la tarde, los disturbios regresaron a los alrededores de la plaza de la República, donde todo había empezado el día anterior. De nuevo, contenedores ardiendo, barricadas formadas con bicicletas de alquiler incendiadas y violentos enfrentamientos con la policía.

A solo dos horas de que empezara la reunión de crisis presidida por el jefe del Estado, Emmanuel Macron, las calles adyacentes a la plaza de la República volvieron a ser el escenario de carreras, lanzamiento de proyectiles y pillajes en tiendas. A medida que pasan las horas, crece la convicción de que gran parte de los disturbios fueron protagonizados por personas ajenas a la protesta estudiantil. Un tipo de violencia más parecido al que se observa cuando hay una victoria del PSG o de la selección francesa que a la que dejaron las protestas de los estudiantes durante la semana anterior. Pillajes, robos, saqueos.

Más información EDITORIAL | Francia ante el caos

La concentración original de este domingo fue dispersada rápidamente con gases lacrimógenos, pero entonces varios grupos se dispersaron por los alrededores, en medio de una creciente confusión que volvió a elevar la tensión en el barrio. En el muelle de Valmy, junto al canal de Saint-Martin, un montón de bicicletas fueron incendiadas, lo que obligó a intervenir a los bomberos. Varios policías se desplegaron para asegurar la zona y fueron recibidos con gritos de “ACAB” (All Cops Are Bastards; Todos los policías son unos bastardos, en inglés). Más allá de esa consideración, lo que sí volvió a ser evidente es que no estaban preparados para repeler disturbios con los que no contaban este domingo.

La tienda de Petite Mendigote, situada en la rue Beaurepaire, en el distrito X de París, fue objeto de actos vandálicos y saqueada por un grupo de individuos. El escaparate del establecimiento fue destrozado y varios hombres pudieron entrar en la tienda. Lo mismo que había ocurrido la noche anterior en centenares de comercios, que fueron desvalijados sin pudor por decenas de vándalos.

Un incendio en la calle Beaurepaire, junto al canal de St Martin, este domingo. Ibrahim Ezzat (Anadolu/Getty Images)

A partir de las 18.30 los camiones de bomberos regresaron al centro para apagar los incendios que los manifestantes provocaron en algunas esquinas para evitar que la policía pudiera circular con sus vehículos. Un grupo de jóvenes, todos vestidos de negro y con grandes bolsas para almacenar los botines de sus pillajes, corría por la calle de Turbigo (en el distrito III) al grito de “Louis Vuitton”. El objetivo era saquear también la gran tienda de lujo.

El presidente del ultraderechista Reagrupamiento Nacional, Jordan Bardella, también se dejó caer por la misma zona horas antes. El delfín de Marine Le Pen, cuyo antisemitismo ha sido puesto de manifiesto recientemente con una serie de mensajes que escribió con 17 años invocando una retahíla de clichés e insultos sobre los judíos, se fue hasta la comisaría del distrito III para ponerse del lado de la policía. “Francia ha sido humillada por una violencia que va en aumento cada vez más. El orden ya no existe en este país”, afirmó el eurodiputado de extrema derecha ante la prensa, antes de ser interpelado en directo por el diputado ecologista Pouria Amirshahi. “Es una vergüenza lo que haces”, le lanzó en un espectáculo televisivo inesperado.

Un manifestante se protege de los gases lacrimógenos, utilizados para dispersar la concentración de este domingo. Ibrahim Ezzat (Anadolu/Getty Images)

Las mismas escenas se repitieron en otras ciudades. Un grupo de unos 50 jóvenes, la mayoría encapuchados, intentó romper el escaparate de una tienda Lacoste en Lyon antes de que interviniera la policía, según publicó Le Figaro. El grupo había salido de la plaza Bellecour en dirección a una calle comercial de la ciudad, pero la policía logró dispersarlo, entre otras medidas, mediante el uso de gases lacrimógenos.

Las fuerzas del orden francesas han detenido por el momento a 2.000 personas por su participación en actos de violencia durante la jornada de protestas del sábado, que en muchos sitios degeneró en enfrentamientos, ataques a edificios públicos y saqueos de comercios.

World.title: Francia ante el caos
World.content:
Las escenas de destrucción en Francia, los saqueos en los comercios y el asalto a edificios públicos poco tienen que ver con las reclamaciones de los estudiantes, y sí con una voluntad de golpear los símbolos de la República y desestabilizar una democracia europea. La funesta jornada del 17 de octubre tardará en olvidarse. Lo que empezó con una convocatoria pacífica por las condiciones en la educación secundaria y el poder adquisitivo derivó en actos de una violencia inusitada provocados por una minoría. Imágenes como la del Ayuntamiento de Limoges en llamas quedarán en la memoria como el momento en el que el caos se adueñó de un país. Pueden achacarse los hechos de estos días a la inacción del Gobierno ante las reivindicaciones sociales y estudiantiles, a la parálisis de un Emmanuel Macron que, tras una década en el poder, es un pato cojo sin margen de maniobra y visceralmente detestado por una parte de la sociedad, o a los bloqueos en una clase política que desde hace décadas ha aplazado las reformas para sacar a la economía del marasmo y reducir las brechas sociales. Ninguno de estos debates debe esconder hoy lo esencial, y es que las protestas son legítimas y en muchos puntos, justificadas, pero la violencia nunca lo es.

02:00 El Ayuntamiento de Limoges, devorado por las llamas en la jornada de protestas en Francia

Francia ya ha acostumbrado al mundo a estas imágenes que en cualquier otra democracia serían inaceptables. Basta recordar las movilizaciones hace unos días en España por la crisis de la vivienda para entender que es posible expresar el descontento en las calles y reivindicar mejoras sociales sin necesidad de recurrir a la violencia, y es posible también canalizarlas en el debate político. Otra particularidad francesa es la de unos cuerpos policiales con un largo historial en el empleo excesivo de la fuerza y que en otras ocasiones, como sucedió el sábado, no han logrado mantener el orden público y evitar el descontrol. Existe además toda una mitología revolucionaria que reemerge en cada movimiento social, como las protestas contra la reforma de las pensiones en los años recientes o los chalecos amarillos, y se remite a momentos que han marcado la identidad de este país, desde la toma de la Bastilla en 1789 y la Comuna de París hasta mayo de 1968. Cuando la violencia exhibe el carácter nihilista de este fin de semana y atenta contra las instituciones públicas, hay un efecto corrosivo que no solo daña a causas y reivindicaciones justas, sino que toca de lleno a la convivencia y la paz civil.

Decía Raymond Aron que los franceses son un pueblo que de vez en cuando hace revoluciones, pero nunca reformas. Después del 17 de octubre, queda claro que la respuesta a la constelación de malestares son las reformas, que es otra manera de decir la política. La prioridad es el restablecimiento del orden, pero ni el presidente ni su Gobierno pueden mantenerse impasibles ante una sociedad en la que los estallidos son periódicos y cada vez más virulentos. Sin mayoría parlamentaria y con las cajas públicas vacías, la capacidad de acción es muy estrecha, pero no hacer nada significa dar más alas a los radicales. A quienes jalean los desórdenes y ven la ocasión para su soñada revolución pendiente, y a quienes, como Marine Le Pen, esperan sacar rédito electoral prometiendo ley y orden. El vicepresidente de EE UU, J. D. Vance, no ha tardado en proclamar en las redes sociales que las imágenes de Francia es una advertencia sobre los peligros de una victoria demócrata en su país. El mensaje es parecido al de Donald Trump tras la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta este verano. Una crisis como esta es combustible para aquellos que, dentro y fuera de Europa, están embarcados en el proyecto de erosionar y destruir nuestras democracias, y aprovecharán cualquier oportunidad.
