World.title: Expert: Trump's recent decisions have nothing to do with midterms
World.content:
Analyzing U.S. President Donald Trump's latest moves that have harmed Ukraine and favored Russia, U.S. politics expert Andreas Kaju admitted he could not explain why the president was making such decisions.

Fuel retailer Alexela's head of energy sales, Tarmo Kärsna, does not believe Russian diesel will help U.S. President Donald Trump achieve his goals of lowering fuel prices and saving American farmers.

"If Russian diesel were brought to the U.S. market, we would be talking about less than a day's consumption. It's a drop in the ocean. Markets are also skeptical today, questioning whether Russia even has the capacity to increase its diesel exports from their current level. After all, exports have fallen sevenfold since January of this year," Kärsna said.

The curtailment of Ukraine's satellite capabilities for striking Russia and defending itself, followed by the decision to abandon planned sanctions, are the latest surprises.

"It is clear that President Trump has taken Russia's side in the war and is clearly acting against Ukraine's interests. This is a very bad development," said European Parliament member Riho Terras (Isamaa).

Why? U.S. politics expert Andreas Kaju said he did not know. The midterm elections have nothing to do with it.

"If he wanted to win elections, he would have acted very differently long ago. What he has been doing consistently over the past year is endorsing extremely unpopular candidates within the Republican Party in various states. As a result, it is entirely possible that Republicans will lose states in the midterm elections that previously would have been unthinkable," Kaju said.

Kaju pointed to an article in the U.S. conservative publication National Review.

"The article argued that it is time for Republicans and Democrats to jointly launch a major congressional investigation into the reasons behind President Trump's Russia policy," Kaju said.

Kaju speculated that such investigations might indeed begin in Congress, including the Senate, after the midterm elections.

World.title: From spreadsheets to autonomous tractors: AI's growing role in farming
World.content:
Artificial intelligence primarily helps farmers process data in their daily operations, but autonomous agricultural robots and drones are no longer the stuff of science fiction either.

According to Airika Verrev, crop and livestock production manager and consultant at Pajo Ranch, AI's capabilities have improved significantly even in the short time she has been using it. This spring, the food producer tried using AI to compile data in Excel, but the technology was not yet up to the task. By the grain harvest season, however, that had changed.

"These days, I no longer create a single Excel spreadsheet myself. I tell AI what I want and what it should look like, and that's it," Verrev said.

She also uses AI to analyze data and find relevant provisions in legislation. Nevertheless, she said the information it provides must be constantly checked.

Marten Madissoo, assistant professor of agricultural engineering at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, confirmed that the technology does not relieve farmers of the responsibility to evaluate its answers.

"We have to bear in mind that AI is simply a useful tool that allows us to make decisions faster, but we still need to be experts ourselves," he said.

More broadly, Madissoo sees significant potential for machine learning and artificial intelligence in the agricultural sector. Potential applications include logistics, organizing the storage and processing of agricultural products and analyzing fields. However, he said there is no one-size-fits-all solution as the potential applications depend largely on the problem being addressed.

One possibility is to make better use of data that farmers already collect for field records, registers and reports.

"We have the advantage of having data spanning several years. By bringing this data together and developing a model to analyze it, we can achieve those gains," Madissoo said.

At the same time, he reiterated the need to combine agricultural and technical expertise. The relevant indicators must be assessed by people familiar with the fields who can define what they want to learn from the data.

From chat bots to field drones

However, chatbots are just the tip of the iceberg. Marten Madissoo coordinates the work of the AI and Robotics Center AIRE at the Estonian University of Life Sciences. The center focuses on opportunities to improve the competitiveness of industrial companies through artificial intelligence and robotics.

As an example of AI's industrial applications, Madissoo pointed to an AIRE demonstration project at meat producer Nõo Lihatööstus, which tested the use of AI for quality control of packaged products moving along a conveyor belt. The system was designed to detect problems such as poorly attached labels, incorrect dates or defects in a product's appearance.

Researchers at the University of Tartu have also used artificial intelligence to identify field islands in aerial photographs and sort grain. Novaator has previously reported on the Estonian University of Life Sciences' experiments with autonomous agricultural machinery.

The AgXeed AgBot autonomous tractor, jointly tested by the Estonian University of Life Sciences and Baltic Agro. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

New solutions involving agricultural drones could soon emerge. An amendment to the Plant Protection Act is currently being considered by the Riigikogu that would allow plant protection products to be sprayed from unmanned aircraft under certain conditions.

According to Madissoo, several autonomous solutions already exist, but their deployment is hindered by both legal restrictions and the need to ensure safety. For example, he said the Estonian University of Life Sciences' field robot is still firmly in the testing phase. The machine needs to be taught the boundaries of fields and where it can operate.

"It's not exactly science fiction, but it will still take some time before we can put all these technologies and capabilities to use," he said.

In his assessment, repetitive tasks with clearly defined procedures are particularly well suited to automation as machine learning can make them more efficient.

Trust but verify

Airika Verrev believes that, in the future, combining data with the help of AI will make farming significantly more precise. For example, AI could analyze aerial and drone photographs to help determine how much fertilizer or plant protection products need to be ordered for the upcoming season. This could help avoid unnecessary spending.

"The savings could actually be quite substantial. Right now, though, we're still estimating how much to order," she said.

According to Verrev, many producers currently use AI primarily as a more advanced search engine. However, she said a lack of time makes it difficult to keep up with new developments.

Madissoo said businesses' willingness to adopt new technology depends primarily on whether the benefits are clear and the investment is justified.

"How much do I need to invest and how quickly will that investment pay for itself?" he said, summing up the key question facing producers.

However, Madissoo believes that an initial experiment does not have to be expensive. Farmers can start with a chatbot and a specific question, then try analyzing their own data and testing the resulting recommendations on a smaller field, for example. For more complex ideas, he recommends seeking support from universities or AIRE.

"At one conference, someone gave a good example of AI adoption: Horses are still around today, but they have absolutely no significance in the transportation sector. It's the same with AI. You can manage without it, but you'll simply fall behind the mainstream. So I encourage people to use it: Trust, but verify," Madissoo said.

World.title: People increasingly not paying hospital fees
World.content:
Since patient visit fees increased last year, more and more people have been falling behind on payments to hospitals. Patients with outstanding debts can no longer see a specialist.

A year and a half ago, the cost of visiting a doctor quadrupled, with patient visit fees rising from €5 to €20 and daily hospital bed fees doubling from €2.50 to €5. Since then, the number of patients owing money to North Estonia Medical Center (PERH) has doubled, while the total amount owed has tripled.

"Daily hospital bed fees account for about 70 percent of the debt, while visit fees, mainly for emergency department visits, account for the remaining 30 percent," said Anneli Habicht, PERH's head of customer service.

According to Habicht, in about half of cases patients simply forget to pay, while the other half have no intention of paying. Before turning to a debt collection agency, the hospital spends a couple of months trying to recover the money itself.

"When we look at which groups are more likely to owe us money, it seems to be older people approaching retirement age, as well as very young adults. In terms of gender, men tend to be more likely to fall behind on payments," Habicht said.

Last year, nearly 2,200 people owed money to Narva Hospital. The amounts involved are generally small and are usually paid after a reminder.

"In the first nine months of this year, the number of debtors has increased by about 25 percent. At the same time, we haven't seen any behavior that would require us to take aggressive action through debt collection agencies or any signs that people are deliberately trying to avoid their obligations," said Narva Hospital CEO Üllar Lanno.

Tartu University Hospital has not experienced the same problems as its counterparts in northern Estonia.

"The hospital still receives most of its revenue for medical treatment through its contract with the Estonian Health Insurance Fund. Patients' out-of-pocket payments account for less than 3 percent of that. We have half a million outpatient visits a year and perhaps 200 to 400 patients need to be sent payment reminders," said Joel Starkopf, a member of Tartu University Hospital's management board.

According to debt collection agency Julianus Inkasso, the number of claims submitted by hospitals has increased by a few percentage points, although some medical institutions have submitted 10 percent more claims.

"When the visit fee was €5, it was a little easier to pay. If you're in a difficult financial situation, €20 is harder to afford. And if you forget to pay on time, finding that extra money later can be more difficult when you're working with a tight household budget," said Merle Laurimäe, CEO of Julianus Inkasso.

More than half of debtors settle their debts within a year of receiving a letter from the collection agency. However, they must also cover late-payment interest and collection fees of up to €30.

"I think the total could rise to around €55 at most, provided you act in time," Laurimäe said.

World.title: Reform Party unveils campaign slogan as PM touts economic growth
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party chair Kristen Michal says Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average, as Reform pledges a clear course in the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the party's council meeting in Tartu on Saturday, Michal said the largest income tax cut in Estonia's history had doubled economic growth.

"Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average," he said, also citing rising wages, consumption, exports and manufacturing, alongside lower unemployment and easing inflation.

"The Reform Party can say with confidence: our plan is working," the prime minister emphasized. "Estonia has been led through a major test and is now on a solid growth path, moving forward even in the face of headwinds."

He noted that wages are rising, with consumer confidence up and people taking home an average of 10 percent more money this year. Defense spending of 5 percent GDP, he added, is also strengthening security and giving families and businesses confidence to plan for the future.

Even the opposition is starting to see that the Reform Party's plan is working, Michal said, accusing Isamaa and the Center Party of already making plans to form a coalition — potentially joined by the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE).

"The Reform Party is their main enemy for a reason: they can only steal Estonia's prosperity and growth if we're out of the picture," the party chair said, emphasizing that the key issue in the March 2027 elections will be whether this prosperity will continue to grow or be taken away from them.

Michal said that incomes must rise faster than prices, as a wealthier Estonia can invest more in education, healthcare, a cleaner environment and a better quality of life.

"No other party in Estonia stands as firmly for the economy, national defense, liberal principles, Estonian-language education and culture, and European values," he said. "These are the foundations of Estonia's future."

'A clear course for the future'

The Reform Party also unveiled its campaign slogan: "A clear course for the future."

Tartu mayor and party council chair Urmas Klaas said it reflects the party's focus on security, economic growth and opportunities for families and businesses.

He recalled that Reform's "Blue, black and white plan" for Estonia, unveiled in March, centers on building a stronger middle class, bolstering security and making greater use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the economy and government.



"We're running for election to ensure that robust security can give families confidence, people's work and knowledge can create prosperity and technology can help businesses grow and the state operate more efficiently," Klaas said.

MP and Reform Party secretary general Kristo Enn Vaga said the slogan emphasizes that Estonia's future is up to its own choices.

"We in the Reform Party want Estonia to be secure and the economy to grow, because that gives people and businesses more opportunities to carry out their plans," Vaga said. "This is the future we want to build."

World.title: Gallery: Public bomb shelter in Tallinn hidden behind woodland mural
World.content:
A street-level public civil defense shelter in the heart of downtown Tallinn has been transformed with a mural featuring Estonian trees and wildlife.

Located next to Kalev Sports Hall in Tiigiveski Park, the modular concrete shelter cannot withstand a direct missile hit, but it can protect around 20 people from blast waves, shrapnel and debris from an explosion as close as 50 meters away.

Similar shelters are already widely used in Ukraine, including in Kramatorsk.

The concrete module, donated by security company Citysec, is also now fully wrapped in a woodland mural by Colorees Art's Helena Hanni and Vahur Agar, featuring a wild hare, a bear family, an owl in flight and a wolf.

While usually kept closed in peacetime, the shelter was open to visitors on Friday, when officials were on hand to explain its features to the public.

Tallinn unveiled a new street-level civil defense shelter on Juhkentali tänav. October 2026. Source: Ellen Rudi/Tallinn Strategic Management Office

City weighs dozens more shelters

Citysec CEO Eduard Rikkas said the module was developed on a 50-50 basis with partners in Ukraine, where the design has already been in use for years.

Deputy Mayor Tiit Terik (Center) said the shelter door can be opened remotely during an emergency, and will unlock automatically if power or communications fail.

The shelter door, he added, will be kept locked in peacetime.

Tallinn has mapped 40 to 50 potential sites for similar shelters, with public procurement to follow if the city decides to order more.

According to the manufacturer, the shelter model installed on Juhkentali tänav costs up to €70,000.

World.title: US firms show increasing interest in developing Iraq’s hydrocarbon resources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Saturday that US firms are showing increasing interest in entering the Iraqi market and developing the country’s oil resources and petroleum industry.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair explained that the Iraqi government supports US corporations’ involvement in the Iraqi market, citing their significant expertise in the oil sector, as well as their ability to transfer knowledge to Iraqi staff.

Several American companies are operating in Iraq, including oil services and consulting firms such as Halliburton, Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and KBR, according to Khudair. He indicated that the ministry reached agreements with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips.

Khudair clarified that the ministry is in negotiations with ExxonMobil to develop the Majnoon oil field, export infrastructure, and a seawater injection project with a capacity of 2.5 million barrels per day to maintain reservoir pressure.

The Iraqi oil minister noted that a deal with Halliburton has been activated to develop the Nahr Bin Umar and Sindbad fields. He added that an agreement with ConocoPhillips has been concluded to develop the Akkas gas field, where Schlumberger is currently operating the project’s first phase.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry activated a deal with Texas-based HKN to develop the Hamrin field, describing the agreement as significant since it develops both oil and gas resources.

Khudair further stated that the Oil Ministry encourages American and European enterprises and works to make the Iraqi market an appealing environment for them.

World.title: US lifts restrictions on Iraqi exchange firms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed on Sunday that the US Treasury Department has lifted restrictions on several Iraqi exchange companies.

The CBI said in a statement that the US Treasury Department removed the restrictions after verifying that these companies met the standards it established, enabling them to resume the sale of US dollars to travelers.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen compliance with regulatory controls and organize the sale of foreign currency in accordance with approved frameworks, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

In late September, the spokesperson for the Iraqi government confirmed that Iraq received a new shipment of US dollars from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Al-Aboudi explained that the step comes within the framework of bilateral understandings reached between Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and US officials during his recent visit to the United States.

The United States halted physical dollar supplies to Iraq in April 2026, including a huge cargo worth $500 million, to force Baghdad to limit the influence of Iran-backed armed groups and minimize illegal financial flow.

Washington decided to keep the supplies going in response to the Iraqi government’s efforts to tighten monitoring on dollar distribution, reduce currency abuse, expand electronic payments, and phase out the traditional currency auction system.

The revenues Iraq generates from international oil exports are officially stored in a designated account under the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank, giving Washington significant structural power over Baghdad’s access to physical cash.

The new funds will be used largely for travel-related activities and foreign transfers approved by the CBI.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister and UK National Security Adviser review security and economic ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi received British National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell in Baghdad on Sunday, October 18, 2026, to discuss expanding bilateral relations between Iraq and the United Kingdom, focusing particularly on defense coordination, intelligence sharing, and economic partnerships.

According to an official communique released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Powell extended congratulations to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi on the parliamentary confirmation and completion of his ministerial lineup.

The British envoy commended Baghdad’s ongoing anti-corruption campaign and structural economic reform agenda, affirming the United Kingdom’s backing for the Iraqi government’s institutional modernization and fiscal stabilization policies.

The discussions also addressed shifting geopolitical dynamics across the Middle East, with both sides underscoring the necessity of close multilateral coordination to de-escalate cross-border frictions.

The meeting emphasized joint diplomatic engagement to resolve underlying causes of regional instability, protect critical supply corridors, and anchor long-term security in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s oil output hits 4.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Eco Iraq, a digital platform that analyzes economic, energy, and environmental data in the country, revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

According to the observatory, Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the military conflict in the Middle East.

Oil output fell to its lowest point in May before gradually recovering in the months that followed.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

Iraq’s oil production in September reached its highest daily rate since the beginning of 2026, signaling a gradual recovery in output following the sharp decline experienced during the months of war in the region.

World.title: Iraq to appoint Al Halbousi and Al Fayyadh as Vice Presidents
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi political factions within the governing State Administration Coalition have reached a preliminary agreement to reactivate the long-dormant positions of Vice President of the Republic, an informed political source revealed on Sunday, October 18, 2026.

Under the emerging cross-party consensus, the leadership posts are slated to be assigned to Taqaddum Party leader and former Parliament Speaker Mohammed Al-Halbousi alongside Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh.

According to the source, the prospective appointments will mirror the financial compensation model adopted for deputy prime ministers, restricting allocations solely to nominal salary entitlements without authorizing supplementary office operational budgets or creating new civil service staff quotas.

The financial restraint is designed to forestall public criticism and prevent administrative expansion within executive payrolls while accommodating broad-based political power-sharing requirements across key coalition partners.

The source noted that restoring the two vice-presidential slots has featured prominently across bilateral consultations and plenary coalition assemblies as a stabilizing mechanism for the current parliamentary cycle.

The political maneuvering follows action taken by the Council of Representatives on Thursday, October 15, when lawmakers ratified three deputy prime ministers and filled eleven ministerial portfolios—including vacant and newly established ministries—within Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s cabinet, while deferring a vote on the Ministry of Migration and Displaced.

World.title: Central Bank of Iraq raises housing loan allocations to 3 trillion dinars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Sunday, October 18, 2026, an expansion of its financial allocations supporting the national housing sector, increasing the designated lending portfolio to three trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $1.97 billion).

The initiative is aimed directly at addressing the high volume of citizen applications seeking to purchase apartments and residential units inside organized housing complexes across Iraqi governorates.

According to an official administrative directive issued by the Central Bank, the decision is enacted pursuant to the provisions of CBI Law No. 56 of 2004, as amended.

The measure triples the previous funding ceiling specified in a prior regulatory directive dated August 22, 2024, raising the aggregate financing cap from one trillion dinars to three trillion dinars while retaining the existing operational terms, repayment criteria, and credit conditions.

The directive instructed the Director General of the relevant specialized lending institution to visit the Central Bank’s headquarters in Baghdad to formally sign the contractual annex required for the allocation increase and finalize administrative protocols.

The liquidity injection expands mortgage-backed real estate credit, stimulates the domestic construction industry, and bridges the acute housing deficit by enabling middle-income citizens to secure homeownership inside modern investment residential compounds.

World.title: PMF’s ammunition depot explodes in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered investigation into the circumstances surrounding an explosion at an ammunition depot in a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) base in the capital, Baghdad, according to the Iraqi Security Media Cell (ISMC).

Al-Zaidi stressed the need to expedite the investigation to find out the specific reasons for the incident and implement all essential safety measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.

The PMF announced on Saturday that five of its members had been wounded following an explosion at an ammunition depot located at one of its bases in eastern Baghdad.

The PMF confirmed in a statement that a fire—triggered by the explosion of a stockpile of damaged ammunition at one of its headquarters in eastern Baghdad—has been brought under control.

The statement indicated that the explosion caused minor injuries to five personnel. Specialized committees have initiated an investigation into the incident’s causes, and the findings will be announced upon the investigation’s conclusion.

During the early stages of the military conflict in the Middle East, which has spilled over into Iraq, several PMF headquarters were targeted in devastating bombings carried out by the United States.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt discuss electricity interconnection project through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed on Saturday approaches to expedite the electricity interconnection project between Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan.

According to a statement released by the Egyptian Foreign Ministry, the meeting took place during Abdelatty’s visit for the 52nd session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers and ahead of al-Zaidi’s scheduled trip to Egypt on November 23.

The meeting addressed measures to improve bilateral cooperation, as well as attempts to de-escalate tensions in the region and promote security and stability.

The two sides discussed the activation of the three countries’ trilateral cooperation mechanism and strategies to advance collaborative projects, notably in electricity interconnection and oil, to promote economic integration and serve the three nations’ common interests.

Abdelatty emphasized the necessity of boosting economic, commercial, and investment relations with Iraq, notably by increasing Egyptian firms’ participation in infrastructure, reconstruction, and development projects.

The Egyptian foreign minister emphasized the possibilities for utilizing Egyptian experience in construction, transportation, energy, agriculture, and pharmaceutical industries.

Abdelatty highlighted the importance of increasing bilateral commerce and facilitating Egyptian products’ access to the Iraqi market.

Additionally, Abdelatty underlined Egypt’s unwavering support for Iraq’s unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, opposing foreign involvement in its internal affairs.

The Egyptian foreign minister also praised the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve national security and reinforce state authority and institutions, including bringing arms under state control.

World.title: Phone on speaker in train? You may be fined, jailed
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a move that could bring relief to railway passengers disturbed by people playing music or watching videos on their phones in speaker mode and check the growing menace, Southern Railway has warned that such behaviour could attract a penalty of Rs 1,000 and lead to removal from railway premises, including coaches.

People persisting with such an act could even face up to six months of jail and up to Rs 5,000 penalty.

Southern Railway has invoked Section 142 of the Railways Act, as amended under the Jan Vishwas Act, to enforce provisions dealing with causing a nuisance.

Officials said that the provision can be invoked by other railway zones and even by Metro systems to check such behaviour, which adversely affects the comfort of other passengers.

As per law, creating a nuisance in Metro rail also attracts a penalty and such persons can be removed from coaches.

Section 270 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines public nuisance as an act that causes common injury, danger, obstruction or annoyance to people using a public right and hence amounts to an offence.

In a circular issued to all its divisions this month and marked to Railway Board, Southern Railway flagged the problem of passengers playing music or audio through speakers at railway stations and inside trains, describing it as a ânuisanceâ.





The circular also referred to a Railway Board communication issued in July 2012 on the use of mobile phones. The board had flagged issues such as âloud talking, lengthy conversationsâ and sound of objectionable ringtones inside coaches and asked all zones to create awareness against such practices.

Official communication from Southern Zone stated, âIn recent times, with the advent of widespread mobile internet access, the playing of videos and other content in speaker mode is highly prevalent in public spaces.

ln the present scenario, there is urgent need to put in place arrangements in order to ensure that travelling passengers are not inconvenienced.â

It has directed its divisions to educate passengers on the relevant legal provisions and discourage them from playing music or videos in speaker mode or engaging in loud conversations while travelling or on railway premises. Awareness campaigns are to be conducted through public address systems in regional languages, Hindi and English. It has said that ticket examiners and other senior officials from commercial division can impose the Rs 1,000 penalty on offenders.

Shinde vows action against threats

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde met Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff at his residence on Sunday night after a firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area, assuring the actor and his family of the state government's support. Photographs from the meeting showed Shroff with bandages on his arm and dressings on his shoulder and chest.Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Shinde said five rounds had been fired during the incident, but the actor was safe. He added that Shroff had sustained injuries to his left hand due to gunpowder and glass shards, while his driver was injured in the incident."This is a major incident... five rounds were fired, but fortunately, he was safe. His driver sustained injuries, and the incident is condemnable. I met with the actor; he has injuries on his left hand caused by gunpowder and shards of glass. Both he and his mother are quite shaken... I have assured them that the state government stands with them in the face of the open threats being directed at public figures... No form of threat will be tolerated," Shinde said.Shinde visited the actor to enquire about his well-being after reports of gunshots being fired while Shroff was leaving a football club on Sunday evening.His mother, Ayesha Shroff, was also present during the meeting. Actor Disha Patani later arrived at Shroff's residence.Condemning the firing, Shinde said the state government would not tolerate attempts to intimidate public figures and assured the Shroff family that the authorities would take necessary steps to address the threat.Drawing a comparison with the gang-related violence witnessed in Mumbai in the 1990s, the deputy chief minister said the police had brought such activities under control and vowed to prevent their resurgence."Such gang wars were quite common in the 90s, but the Mumbai Police put an end to them in 1995... These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," he said.Shinde's visit came amid concerns over the firing incident, with the state government assuring the actor and his family of its support. The police have maintained that Shroff was safe and had not suffered any gunshot wounds.

and Ashutosh Ranka was put off Sunday after the special executive magistrate failed to arrive at the scheduled time, and later recused himself citing threat to his life.

World.title: Omar Abdullah seeks action over attack on J&K-bound bus in Haryana
World.content:
SRINAGAR: The J&K govt and political parties in the union territory have unitedly condemned the attack on a Srinagar-bound bus in Haryana.

âThis unfortunate incident should never have taken place. I hope the Haryana govt led by Nayab Singh Saini and Haryana Police catch the culprits & take action to ensure these things donât happen again,â Omar wrote on X.

Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq called the incident as âdisturbing.â âReports of threats against J&K-registered vehicles are causing concern among people. Those in authority must ensure the safety of Kashmiri travellers and take swift and strict legal action against those responsible,â he said.

World.title: Espionage case on Army officer’s wife, lens on ‘China links’
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a case and started a probe against a Jammu-based Army officerâs wife for allegedly collecting and sharing sensitive information with foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, sources said Sunday.

The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. She allegedly used AI tools ChatGPT and Claude to write papers on sensitive security issues for Chinese intelligence operatives suspected to have contacted her posing as academicians. The information was allegedly passed on through encrypted communication (online) mediums.

The woman married the major-rank officer in 2023, a year after finishing a course in international governance from Geneva.

She got a Masterâs degree from a Bengaluru university in 2021.

A joint team of officers, including some from a central intelligence agency, intercepted the woman at Jammu railway station on Oct 14 when she was reportedly preparing to board a train to Pathankot. She was stopped and taken to a nearby military station for questioning, officials said. This followed a case filed at Jammuâs Gandhi Nagar Police Station under Official Secrets Act, and BNS sections relating to criminal conspiracy and offences against national sovereignty.





A DSP assigned to lead the probe has questioned the woman, seizing her phone and extracting data that purportedly showed documents on sensitive subjects. The accused claimed her material was based entirely on open-source research supplemented by the AI platforms.

The officials made it clear that despite being booked, the woman has not been arrested yet. Her interrogation indicated that she had interacted with several foreign nationals during her UN internship, including a Chinese national with whom she allegedly maintained contact through WhatsApp, the officials said.

In 2024, she was in contact via social media with a Malaysian consultant allegedly working for Chinese intelligence agencies, the officials added.

Preliminary investigations indicate the Chinese operatives initially made the woman write articles on environmental and geopolitics issues before gradually goading her to switch to defence matters. Investigators suspect she may have fallen into an âintellectual trapâ, not realising that those approaching her as academicians were actually operatives trying to extract sensitive information.

Investigators are examining whether the woman engaged in systematic information-sharing under the guise of freelance research, adding a comprehensive forensic examination of her digital devices and financial transactions is on to establish the exact nature of the shared material, the officials said.

World.title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
World.content:
CJI Surya Kant inaugurates the Ladakh HC bench in Leh Sunday

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level â an altitude no other HC can ever match.Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, âI am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.âJ&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein.Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many. Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh.âBut a name on a courtâs letterhead is not the same as a court on oneâs doorstepâ¦ The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,â he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani.But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services.âAccess to justice, after all, begins not in the courtâs compound, but at the litigantâs door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,â he said.In an unprecedented gesture, the CJI said, âOnce video-conferencing facilities are adequately available to the lawyers of the Ladakh bench, Supreme Court shall list all matters coming from Ladakh on a single day, and hear them on a day-to-day basis, also through videoconferencing.ââSomewhere in Ladakh today, in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra, there is a young child who will one day argue her first case in this court, and perhaps even sit on its bench as a judge. When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh but taken root here,â the CJI said.

World.title: 'Barged in, cut power': AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj claims Delhi Police harassing Bengali community in CR Park
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Saurabh Bharadwaj has accused Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park), alleging that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment.

He also warned that restrictions on Puja celebrations could lead to overcrowding, drawing a parallel with the Kolkata stampede that killed 17 people on Saturday.

In a post on X addressed to Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) state president claimed that the community and Puja organisers were facing unprecedented harassment.

âAttention @LtGovDelhi saab, Delhi Police officers are harassing the Bengali community and CR Park Durga Puja Committees like never before.

This community is one of the most decent and well-educated sections of Delhi,â he wrote.

Questioning the alleged disparity in the treatment of different cultural events, Bharadwaj referred to the Delhi government's position on allowing shops and businesses to operate round the clock and said most Ram Leela celebrations were permitted to continue past midnight.

âWhen the Delhi Govt talks about 24x7 businesses and shops, and most Ram-leelas are allowed past midnight, why the stepmotherly treatment for the Bengali community?â he asked.





Bharadwaj also alleged that police constables entered the B Block Durga Puja pandal on Saturday and cut its electricity connections. âYesterday, police constables barged into the B Block Durga Puja pandal and forcibly cut the electrical connections, damaging their equipment. This is not done,â he said.

In another post on X, Bharadwaj criticised the BJP over the reported West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy and raised concerns about crowd management at the Puja pandals.

âBJP has learnt nothing from the West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy,â he wrote.

He claimed that lakhs of people, including Bengalis and non-Bengalis, visit CR Park's Puja pandals every year, particularly in the evenings. He further alleged that Puja committees had been told that pandals and loudspeakers could operate only until 10 pm this year, compared with midnight last year.

âSqueezing the evening window by 2 hours will cause crowd swell and chaos.

This could lead to a West Bengal-type situation, and the government will prosecute puja committees to hide its own shortcomings,â Bharadwaj alleged.

Meanwhile, the Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II and adjoining areas of South Delhi from October 16 to 20, between 4 pm and midnight, citing the expected influx of visitors and limited road space around the pandals.

Private vehicles belonging to visitors and devotees will not be allowed to enter CR Park and Greater Kailash-II during the restricted hours. Commuters have been advised to use the Delhi Metro, with taxi and auto-rickshaw drop-off points designated at Greater Kailash and Nehru Enclave Metro stations. The police has also warned that illegally parked vehicles or those obstructing traffic may be towed and prosecuted.

The restrictions are scheduled to remain in place until October 20.

World.title: France protests: Macron vows to hold accountable those who ‘sought to bring down the Republic’
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday (October 18, 2026) voiced the public's “anger” and “shame” over rioting and looting during nationwide protests against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. At least 1,800 people have been arrested.

“Those who looted will have to pay back for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable,” Mr. Macron said in a televised address to the nation.

He blamed “unrestrained violence” on “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”

Mr. Macron has earlier held an emergency meeting with senior government officials, a day after masked groups set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities. He said he had instructed prefects to work with Mayors to protect public buildings and businesses in the coming weeks, including by banning protests when necessary.

Flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall in the city of Limoges, in central France, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building.

Hundreds of protesters gathered again on Sunday (October 18, 2026) at the Place de la République in Paris amid a heavy police presence. Officers used tear gas as tensions flared sporadically in the neighbourhood, with small groups of people trying to set bicycles and trash bins on fire.

“The right to protest is a fundamental right. Deliberately and collectively sowing disorder through violence is not,” Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez wrote on X, citing the looting of hundreds of businesses in cities including Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux.

About 5,50,000 people took part in protests across France, according to authorities, while organisers put the figure at about 8,00,000. Demonstrators answered calls from a labour union, student organisations and activists hoping to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 to protest social injustice.

Mass protests in France are often marred by violence on the fringes of otherwise peaceful marches, leading to clashes with police. The arrest tally reported Sunday (October 18, 2026) approached the nearly 2,000 recorded nationwide during a single day of yellow vest protests in December 2018.

One person died of a heart attack, Paris police said in a statement, without providing details. The Paris prosecutor's office said it was investigating.

Parisians deplore shattered shops and a damaged square

Dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass littered the area around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday (October 18, 2026). Looting and damage were also reported in other tourist and shopping districts.

Paris police said 855 people were arrested in the capital region. The city's prosecutor's office said 557 remained in police custody.

“I am actually stunned by the level of destruction and violence that was expressed,” said government employee Marie Peyreigne, 57, wondering what had led to the mayhem.

Parisians inspecting the damage photographed the partially dismantled base of the square's central monument, a statue of Marianne, a symbol of France.

Jean Foissy, 74, said he had wanted to join the protest but encountered “a wall of riot police and fires everywhere” and returned home.

“I was very scared,” he said. “I've been a Parisian since I was born, so when I got here, it almost made me want to cry because I find it so bad, it hurts me.”

Margaux Eude, 26, said she supported the protest movement but “didn't think it would escalate like this.”

“It's the troublemakers who came, and it breaks my heart because it delegitimises the movement,” she said.

Political leaders trade blame ahead of presidential election

Political leaders across the spectrum sought to parlay the fallout of Saturday's (October 17, 2026) riots into political capital, looking ahead to next spring's presidential election.

Far-right leader and presidential hopeful Marine Le Pen criticized Macron's centrist government as “exhausted, disoriented and seemingly incapable of doing anything other than commenting on its own powerlessness,” in a video posted Sunday on social media.

Far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, for his part, accused Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu of “playing with fire,” alleging that “by banking on degradation, you have only succeeded in uniting all youths and workers' unions.”

Mr. Mélenchon, who joined the Paris march Saturday, insisted that “my message is clear: those who share our fight have no business in looting or destruction.”

U.S. President Donald Trump posted “France is burning!” on his Truth Social platform, apparently linking the unrest to “the immigration of people from an entirely different world.”

“Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” he wrote.

French authorities and police have not linked immigrants to the rioting and have repeatedly attributed some of the violence to “radical far-left groups” and other people who joined to loot.

World.title: Morning Digest: Public audit in two booths finds over 100 voters wrongly marked Delhi SIR; Police detain Sahil Wakode’s parents from protest site, and more
World.content:
Delhi SIR: Public audit in two booths find over 100 voters wrongly marked absent, shifted, or dead

At least 100 voters from two polling booths in Delhi’s Okhla constituency were found to have been wrongly classified as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, a public audit covering 258 households over seven days found.

IIT-B student death case: Police detain Sahil Wakode’s parents, clear protest site

The Mumbai Police on Sunday (October 18, 2026) detained several students along with the parents of Sahil Wakode, an IIT Bombay student who died by suicide, from the protest site in front of the institution. Earlier, the police detained 10 students from the protest site before the parents arrived. These students were later released and returned to join the gathering, after which Ravindra and Sonali Wakode reached the institute.

Actor Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt in Juhu firing incident; suspect detained

Actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after a shooting incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday (October 18, 2026) evening; two individuals, including his driver, sustained injuries in the attack. The police have detained one suspect in connection with the incident. According to Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg, the incident occurred around 7 p.m. as Shroff was leaving the place after work. His driver, Firdaus, suffered an injury to his left hand, while another bystander, Mr. Chauhan, was also injured and taken to a local hospital for treatment.

Eight workers mowed down by speeding car in Punjab’s Sangrur; 12 injured

Eight workers were killed, and 12 others sustained injuries after a car ran over them on Lehragaga-Jakhar road in Punjab’s Sangrur district on Sunday (October 18, 2026), police said. The incident occurred near Alisher village when a group of more than 20 workers enrolled under Viksit Bharat Guarantee Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-G RAM G) — several of them women — were engaged in some work. Some of them were sitting along the road.

Majority of victims in Kolkata Durga Puja stampede are women, children

The majority of victims in the Kolkata Durga Puja stampede were women and children. The list of 19 deceased persons shared by the police on Sunday (October 18, 2026) includes 13 females, two of them minors. Among the youngest victims of the tragedy were three boys - a seven-year-old from Bihar, a 13-year-old from Agarpara, North 24 Parganas, and a 14-year-old from Purba Bardhaman.

Tiger Shroff firing incident: Opposition targets Fadnavis over ‘deteriorating’ law and order

The Opposition on Sunday (October 18, 20) criticised the Maharashtra government over a firing attempt on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, alleging that law and order in the city and State had deteriorated. Shroff escaped unhurt after gunmen opened fire near Pushpa Park in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday (October 18) evening. His driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured in the incident, police said.

Bomb threat forces airliner from Tel Aviv to divert to Bulgaria

A bomb threat against an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday (October 18, 2026) forced the plane to divert to Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian authorities and the airline. The Austrian Airlines crew decided to make an emergency landing in Sofia after reportedly receiving a bomb threat as they neared Romania, Bulgaria’s Transport Ministry said in a statement, adding that the passengers were evacuated from the aircraft after landing.

Israeli PM Netanyahu warns of potentially hostile future U.S. President, calls for alliances with India, Latin America

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday (October 18, 2026) warned that a future U.S. President could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries such as India and those in Latin America to strengthen his country’s position. Mr. Netanyahu made the remarks at an event where he presented his security doctrine, nine days before Israel’s October 27 election.

Venezuela Opposition alliance confirms Nobel laureate Machado as leader

An alliance of Venezuelan Opposition parties on Sunday (October 18, 2026) confirmed exiled Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado as its leader, increasing pressure on interim authorities to allow her return. The coalition’s announcement comes as one Opposition faction engages in political transition talks with the interim government, following the U.S. ouster of longtime leader Nicolas Maduro.

World.title: Temple development works worth ₹2,500 crore under way across Telangana: Bhatti Vikramarka
World.content:
The State government is spending around ₹2,000 crore on developing temples along the Godavari and riverbank areas ahead of the Godavari Pushkaralu scheduled for next year, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka said on Sunday.

He said ₹276 crore had been allocated for the development of Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy temple at Bhadrachalam and ₹354 crore for the Sri Gnana Saraswati temple at Basar.

In all, temple development works were being undertaken across the State at an estimated cost of ₹2,500 crore, he added.

Mr. Vikramarka was speaking after laying the foundation stone for a road at an estimated cost of ₹44 crore at Nacharam village in Enkoor mandal of Khammam district. He also offered prayers at the Adbhutha Venkateswara Swamy temple in the village.

He said the road would ensure easier access for devotees and create employment and livelihood opportunities for local youth.

Highlighting the Congress government’s welfare initiatives, he said fine rice was being distributed to 1.06 crore families, while Rajiv Aarogyasri provided free medical treatment of up to ₹10 lakh per family. Rythu Bharosa assistance was being extended to 71 lakh farmers, and 53 lakh families were receiving free electricity for consumption of up to 200 units a month.

Other initiatives included interest-free loans to women, social security pensions for eligible beneficiaries, free bus travel for women and Indiramma houses for the poor, he said.

In the education sector, the State government was implementing a breakfast scheme for 27 lakh students of government schools, establishing Advanced Technology Centres and taking up construction of Young India Integrated Residential Schools in every Assembly constituency at an estimated cost of ₹200 crore.

The government was also undertaking road development works worth ₹90,000 crore across the State and taking steps to ensure uninterrupted power supply despite electricity demand exceeding 20,000 MW, he said.

Referring to the potential impact of El Nino, Mr. Vikramarka urged people to conserve water and appealed to farmers to monitor groundwater levels and use agricultural pumps judiciously.

World.title: IUML Keralam chief Sadikali Thangal downplays row over Waqf board reconstitution
World.content:
Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal on Sunday downplayed the controversy over the reconstitution of the State Waqf Board.

He told the media here that those who had grievances were free to approach the court. Mr. Thangal maintained that all Muslim organisations had been given representation in the board and those left out could be considered for membership in other bodies.

“The bodies such as the Hajj Committee and the Madrasa Welfare Fund Board are yet to be reconstituted by the government. Those who have not been included in the Waqf board will be considered for such bodies,” Mr. Thangal said.

Amid criticism

His comments come against the backdrop of the criticism from the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama faction led by Sunni scholar Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliar that they had not been given fair representation in the board.

Responding to allegations that Sunni organisations managing a large number of Waqf properties, such as the Kanthapuram faction, had been denied proper representation, Mr. Thangal said the board would address all these concerns without any discrimination. He said the chairman of the Hajj Committee is still a representative of the Kanthapuram faction and that the United Democratic Front (UDF) government did not change that arrangement.

He also maintained that the reconstituted Waqf board included representatives associated with the Samastha. “There are two representatives from the Samastha. One is the chairman himself, who is among its prominent members. Musthafal Faisy is also from the Samastha,” Mr. Thangal said.

World.title: Elaborate arrangements made for Teppotsavam in Vijayawada on October 20
World.content:
Elaborate arrangements are being made for the Teppotsavam (float festival), the concluding ceremony of the nine-day Dasara Navaratri celebrations of the Kanaka Durga temple atop Indrakeeldari in Vijayawada, in the Krishna River on October 20.

Devotees are excited for the Teppotsavam this year as it was cancelled in the last two years due to the floods in the Krishna.

Officials of endowments, police, irrigation and other departments are making elaborate arrangements for the boat ride of Goddess Kanaka Durga and Lord Malleswara Swamy.

The Hamsa Vahanam, on which the deities will take a ride on the Krishna river, has been decked up.

The officials conducted a trial run of the Hamsa Vahanam (boat) on Sunday.

The police have deployed personnel on the ghats as a precautionary measure and the Irrigation Department has deployed expert swimmers at the bathing ghats.

The Hamsa Vahanam and the Durga and Punnami ghats have been illuminated for the festival.

The NTR Commissionerate Police will take the deities in a procession along the Brahmana Veedhi. Shami Puja and Paruveta will also be performed in Jammidoddi as part of the rituals.

World.title: Two held for sexual exploitation of minor of minor in Kovalam spa
World.content:
The Thiruvananthapuram City Police have arrested two men in connection with the alleged exploitation of a 16-year-old girl at a spa in Kovalam.

The Kovalam police identified the accused persons as Nishanth, 46, of Poovar, and Sajith Kumar, 47, of Mavelikkara.

The victim, a native of Andhra Pradesh, is suspected to have been brought to Kovalam in July by her maternal aunt and the aunt’s husband, who were responsible for her care after her parents’ death.

The investigators suspect that the relatives used forged documents to falsely establish that the girl was 20 years old. An Aadhaar card in her possession, which indicated that age, was found to be fake, according to the police.

The girl had purportedly been working at various spas since July and was subjected to sexual exploitation. Her ordeal came to light after she reportedly fell in love with a man at one of the spas and attempted to flee. She disclosed details of the alleged abuse during counselling.

The girl’s relatives, who are accused of trafficking and exploiting her, are believed to have returned to Andhra Pradesh. The Kovalam police have launched an investigation to trace them.

Meanwhile, the City police are pursuing the suspected involvement of a health official in the operations of a spa. Leads of possible benami transactions emerged during an examination of Nishanth’s mobile phone, an official said.

In wake of the incident, the Kerala Police conducted a Statewide crackdown on spas and wellness centres. centers. The police inspected 586 spas and registered 14 cases for various violations. Five persons were taken into custody during the raid. Besides, as many as 44 spas that operate in violation of statutory regulations have been served notices.

World.title: 60-day pause on Russia sanctions to analyse global impact: Rubio
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said the waiver from sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries, including India, was a 60-day pause to analyse the global impact of the measure.

Mr. Rubio was responding to questions on Saturday at Joint Base Andrews near here as he left for a six-day tour of Uzbekistan and India.

“I think the President wants to take the 60 days to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the U.S. economy,” Mr. Rubio said in response to a question on the waivers granted by Mr. Trump under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act or the Graham Act.

On Friday (October 16, 2026), Mr. Trump waived key provisions of the Graham Act that authorised punitive tariffs on countries purchasing Russian oil, offering relief to India.

FULL REMARKS: Secretary Rubio Answers Questions Before Departing from Joint Base Andrews for Uzbekistan and India. https://t.co/fuJqBfcfKT — Department of State (@StateDept) October 18, 2026

The executive order states that the waivers will remain in effect until the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.

Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago resort near Miami, Mr. Trump said his decision to waive sanctions under the Graham Act would benefit the U.S.

“A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out,” he said.

“It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage,” Mr. Trump said.

Mr. Rubio said when the Graham Act was passed, the waivers were put in to study the different things going around the world such as the pressure on global energy supplies due to the Iran war, the attack of Houthis in Saudi Arabia and the Ukraine-Russia war.

“So I think you have to take all of that into account and weigh it against each other,” Mr. Rubio said.

“Then you've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next,” said the Secretary of State, who is scheduled to be in India on Monday (October 19).

‘Key ally of U.S.’

Mr. Rubio said India was an important ally and partner of the United States, and the President needed that period of time to study all this and figure out what the right combination was.

Mr. Trump’s decision to waive sanctions on Russia came under fire from the Republicans and Democrats, who last month came together to overwhelmingly pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

Senator Darline Graham, a Republican from South Carolina, also criticised Mr. Trump for exempting Russia from a sanctions law that was championed by and named after her late brother Lindsey.

“Personally, I would choose to put the pressure on Russia to end the war and get gas prices down, because I don’t trust [President Vladimir] Putin, and I don’t trust Russia,” said Ms. Graham, who was endorsed by Mr. Trump to fill in the Senate seat that fell vacant due to the death of her brother.

“Beyond irresponsible,” said Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, on social media.

“What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisors not understand,” Mr. Tillis said.

“It's unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine,” he said.

Mr. Tillis said if Mr. Trump wanted to actually bring down energy prices, he should resolve the Iran war, which was largely blamed for the spike at the pump, and not do a solid for Mr. Putin.

Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas said, “Lindsey would be appalled,” referring to the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who worked endlessly on the bill before he died this summer.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, Democrat from Massachusetts, said Trump was thumbing his nose at Congress and enabling Mr. Putin to continue his war of aggression. She urged her colleagues to take action to reverse course.

World.title: Vadaanya Talent Test 2026 to be held in Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai districts on December 13
World.content:
Vadaanya Janaa Society, an NGO established in 2010 to support underprivileged and talented students from rural areas, will be organising the Vadaanya Talent Test 2026 on December 13, 2026, in Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts of Andhra Pradesh.

The announcement was made during a programme held at AF Ecology Centre, Anantapur, where the Vadaanya Talent Test 2026 poster and question booklet were released. Necessary permissions for the conduct of the examination were obtained from the respective District Collectors and District Education Officers, Vadaanya founder Ashok Padapati said.

As part of its preparations for the 2026 examination, Vadaanya released the question booklet containing question papers from the previous five years. The booklet aims to help students understand the examination pattern and prepare effectively.

The organisers expect approximately 10,000 students from government schools across the two districts to participate. Online registrations would begin on November 1, 2026. Registration details, eligibility criteria, and examination updates can be found on the website: www.vadaanya.org.

Established in 2010, Vadaanya Janaa Society has been working to improve educational opportunities for rural students through scholarships, mentoring, academic support, and talent identification initiatives. Over the years, the organisation has supported and guided thousands of students in pursuing their educational goals.

Several students identified through Vadaanya’s Talent Test have achieved good results in competitive examinations such as JEE Main and secured admissions to prestigious institutions, including IITs and IISc Bengaluru.

Y. V. Mallareddy of AF Ecology Centre and other guests attended the programme and appreciated Vadaanya’s efforts to promote education among rural students.

The examination aims to identify talented students who have studied in government schools up to Class 10 and provide them with guidance and encouragement to pursue higher education at leading institutions such as IITs, NITs, and IISc.

World.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition engages with Centre on counterterrorism
World.content:
PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and engage with the Centre on a plan, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end.

He made these remarks while speaking to the media in Karachi, where he was visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the Karsaz bombing.

His statement comes a week after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI, which was in power in KP and in opposition in the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

“If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor’s rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism,” Bilawal said on Sunday, referring to the PTI-led opposition.

He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and “we agree on a plan” to do so, the emergency and governor’s rule in KP could end.

“If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister (Sohail Afridi) is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them,” Bilawal said.

“That is why we supported the government’s decision to impose governor’s rule in KP.”

He stressed that the party would “join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists”.

In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where “terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar”.

He regretted that when the Taliban came to power in Kabul in 2021, the Pakistani government at that time “also decided to invite the terrorists who were in Afghanistan to come back and live in our Swat, our Malakand, our former tribal areas”. He was seemingly referring to then-prime minister Imran’s plans to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan in the country.

Bilawal went on to say that terrorists who were in jail in Pakistan were also freed. “Today, Pakistan is suffering the losses from these wrong decisions,” he lamented.

He added that the country had now once again reached the point where “some forces want to take down Pakistan’s flag in Swat” and there was a fight against terrorism ongoing across the entire country, while security forces, law enforcers and the public were being targeted.

However, he claimed, in the province where the highest number of terrorist incidents were taking place — KP — its chief minister had pledged that he would not face the terrorists.

In response to a question about the Karsaz bombing, the PPP chairman remarked that the greatest loss was caused when terrorist incidents were not taken seriously.

He said that the PPP had “prepared entire society” to fight terrorism by creating an environment for counterterrorism operations in 2008, when the party was in power. After that, he said, when the National Action Plan was introduced, the PPP adopted a holistic approach towards bringing changes in institutions to assist with combatting terrorism.

He emphasised that success was achieved when “every citizen” of Pakistan joined the fight against terrorism, saying, “Today as well, we will make efforts to create an environment where we are all united, and will fight the terrorists together.”

Answering further questions, he said Pakistan was facing a “historic economic crisis”.

“It appears that the situation will worsen. Our priority is to address this economic crisis, and to do that, we will have to fight terrorism as well,” he added.

He said efforts should also be made to improve the democratic and electoral system in Pakistan.

For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this.

He said the PPP also made an effort to improve the democratic system by pushing for electoral reforms. To this end, the federal government had decided to establish an electoral reforms committee in the National Assembly, adding that he had invited the opposition to play their part in that committee as well.

“If they say that democracy is weak in this country, they should help us to strengthen it,” the PPP chairman said.

He added, “If we can create such an environment, we will be in a better position to fight terrorists.”

Bilawal also said KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had been nominated by the PPP for the office of governor, but “constitutionally, he is now a representative of the federal government”.

He said Kundi reported to the federal government, but “I will keep talking to him and keep advising him; in principle, though, he is now working together with the federal government”.

Responding to a question regarding a potential “compromise” with the opposition, Bilawal said, “You say ‘compromise’ like it’s a bad word […] Compromise and politics go hand in hand.”

He stressed that ex-PM Benazir had always strived for compromises during her political career, adding that she knew that one could reach “extremes” if they remained a revolutionary or an activist who only protested rather than working for their cause.

“We had to solve our issues and lift the public and our workers out of difficulty,” Bilawal said about the PPP’s past tenures in government. He asserted that it was the result of the PPP’s “compromises” that led to the end of Gen Pervez Musharraf’s dictatorship, as well as the passage of the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment.

“We (the PPP) are not in the federal government. Nor do we have a majority in Parliament,” he said. “But [we have to see] how we can conduct politics in the space we have.”

New provinces

Answering a question regarding the creation of new provinces, Bilawal stated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi knew “clearly” what the PPP and President Asif Ali Zardari’s policy was regarding new provinces or administrative units, and that this was “not possible without the president’s signature”.

Naqvi’s July remarks calling for new provinces and reforms in the current governance system had ignited an animated debate across the country. The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any possible division of the province.

Bilawal stressed that the PPP’s position was clear: that they could be created in accordance with the Constitution and law if the provincial assembly agreed. The Sindh Assembly, amid a boycott by the opposition, adopted a resolution last month rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units.

“Where there is consensus and it is not a political stunt, if there is no other purpose behind it … why aren’t provinces being made there?” the PPP chairman said, giving the example of Gilgit-Baltistan.

“If we really want this to be implemented, it must only be implemented where the provinces want this,” he stressed, noting that the entire GB Legislative Assembly had passed a resolution with consensus for the region’s constitutional rights.

Bilawal requested politicians, whether on the treasury or opposition benches, not to politicise the issue of terrorism or create controversy out of steps taken to combat it, but rather to play their role in fighting it.

Bilawal also spoke about Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, saying he had the right to criticise the government’s policies, and that there should certainly be room for difference of opinion in the country.

He said the PPP had always imposed emergency through constitutional and legal means.

“In fact, during the 2008–2013 government, when emergency rule was imposed in Balochistan, it was also because of the terrorism situation, and governor’s rule was imposed there against the PPP’s own government.

“If the PPP thought only of itself, how would it have removed its own government?“

He said Fazl’s party has also been affected by terrorist attacks, so he hoped the JUI-F chief would criticise the PPP politically as much as he wished, but also condemn the terrorists.

Bilawal added that if Fazl made an effort, harmony between the government and the opposition could be achieved.

World.title: Two moments of madness cost Sri Lanka as Pakistan win tri-series opener after Salman Ali Agha century
World.content:
Sri Lanka were cruising.

Only 53 runs stood between them and a flying start in the One-day International tri-series opener against Pakistan after Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage’s 119-run stand.

The dew that made the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium outfield relentlessly slick on Sunday night had also deprived Pakistan’s pacers of the chance to extract reverse swing from the old ball.

Then came two moments of madness. Liyanage, who had looked composed throughout his innings, chipped Haris Rauf casually to Babar Azam at long-on before Dasun Shanaka, who had threatened to take the game away from Pakistan, heaved Shaheen Shah Afridi to the same fielder in the same position. In the space of four balls, Sri Lanka unravelled.

Naseem Shah then had Sachindu Colombage caught behind, Eshan Malinga was run out after a mix-up, and Haris cleaned up Asitha Fernando to seal a 37-run win for Pakistan, who had earlier posted 305 thanks to Salman Ali Agha’s third ODI century.

Salman celebrated his return to the Pakistan side after his unceremonious axing from the Test team two months ago with a composed 107 off 90 balls, including 10 fours and a six.

Pakistan’s innings, however, finished with a flourish from Sri Lanka’s bowlers, who conceded only 36 runs while taking five wickets in the last five overs. Eshan Malinga led the charge with figures of 4-46.

After openers Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub fell to Dilshan Madushanka, Babar Azam and Saad Baig steadied the innings with a 74-run partnership for the third wicket.

Malinga broke through by bouncing out Babar for 45 and Saad for 39, bringing Salman and Hasan Nawaz together.

The pair added 97, with Salman gradually increasing the tempo after initially settling in. He brought up his half-century in the 35th over, rotating the strike and punishing loose deliveries.

Salman Agha plays a shot during the tri-series one-day international (ODI) cricket match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 18, 2026. — AFP

Hasan supplied the acceleration with two sixes off Sachindu Colombage, including a powerful slog sweep over cow corner.

Salman then took charge, pulling Dasun Shanaka through the leg side before launching Malinga’s slower delivery over long-off for six.

He reached three figures in the 45th over, finding the boundary through deep midwicket before edging a full delivery past the infield to third man.

Hasan fell for 37, caught by Pavan Rathnayake at short midwicket off Asitha Fernando, who also removed Arafat Minhas for 18.

Salman departed for 107 at 279-6, mistiming a lofted shot to Shanaka at long-on, and Sri Lanka seized control.

Malinga dismissed Faheem Ashraf and trapped Naseem Shah lbw in the next over, while accurate yorkers restricted Pakistan’s lower order. Haris was run out for a duck in the final over, leaving Pakistan all out for 305 in 49.5 overs.

Sri Lanka’s reply began poorly. Shaheen and Naseem made early inroads, reducing the visitors to 91-4 and leaving the chase in need of repair.

But as the ball and outfield grew wetter, Pakistan’s bowlers struggled to make the ball grip, allowing Rathnayake and Liyanage to rebuild with patience and calculated aggression.

Rathnayake initially played watchfully before cutting Arafat Minhas late through deep point and pulling Saim Ayub to the deep midwicket boundary.

He raised his maiden ODI half-century with a single off Arafat in the 31st over, then pulled two short balls from Shaheen over square leg in successive deliveries.

Liyanage offered stability at the other end, rotating the strike and punishing anything loose. He drove Naseem through the gap between mid-off and extra cover before dancing down the track to hammer Arafat straight down the ground.

Their running between the wickets kept the scoreboard moving as Pakistan struggled to find a breakthrough.

Faheem Ashraf (R) bowls as Sri Lanka’s Dasun Shanaka watches during the tri-series one-day international (ODI) cricket match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi on October 18, 2026. — AFP
